item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] PC7 Model: Dynamics of Expanding and Contracting Soft Robots using Piece-wise Constant 7D Deformation Based on Similarity Transformation Group
item.description: arXiv:2610.14586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a novel soft robot model named piece-wise constant 7D deformation (PC7) model that can represent expanding and contracting deformation of, for example, artificial muscle actuator. In the proposed model, we newly define the 7D deformation vector based on SIM(3) - 3D similarity transformation group - whereas a 6D deformation vector was defined for Cosserat rod based on SE(3) - the special Euclid group - in the piece-wise constant strain (PCS) model proposed in the previous study. The additional dimension of the 7D deformation vector represents expanding and contracting deformation, which comes from the scaling parameter in SIM(3). Common mathematical properties between SE(3) and SIM(3) allow us to directly extend the kinematics and dynamics of the PCS model to those of the PC7 model. In particular, we derive the dynamical equation of the PC7 model based on Euler-Poincare equation in a mathematically precise manner. We validate the proposed model through dynamical simulations assuming a thin cylinder structure or McKibben-type artificial muscle actuator.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Flow-Support-Weighted Proposals for Test-Time Verified VLA Policies
item.description: arXiv:2610.14588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Test-time sampling promises to turn one action prediction into a set of distinct executable candidates that a verifier can choose among. Downstream fine-tuning works against that promise. A vision-language-action model trained to solve one task distribution concentrates its flow-matching decoder around the dominant demonstrated action, so repeated samples differ only marginally and the verifier receives many copies of one decision. We call this proposal contraction and identify it as a key constraint on test-time scaling: repeated samples can remain highly redundant as the candidate budget grows. Action Dynamic Sampling (ADS) alleviates the constraint on the proposal side, during training. At each training step, ADS integrates $K$ additional trajectories from the current policy under fresh base noise, scores each by the flow support along its path with a Hutchinson trace estimator, and corrects the policy's local action distribution toward this weighted set through a detached finite-set KL term. Training cost rises; deployment cost is unchanged. Across simulation and four physical-robot tasks, ADS raises proposal spread without the success penalty that Gaussian perturbation incurs, lifts oracle best-of-8 success on RoboCasa from 57.6% to 63.0%, improves fixed verifiers by 2.4 to 4.9 points in simulation, and raises TokenPB by up to 13.0 points on real-world manipulation.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Attribute-Centric Vision-Language Alignment for Fine-Grained Gait Understanding
item.description: arXiv:2610.14589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Walking sequences reveal human-interpretable attributes related to body structure, posture, and motion. Gait attribute recognition provides a concrete route to fine-grained gait understanding by predicting these attributes. However, existing benchmarks provide limited fine-grained annotations, while classifier-based gait attribute recognition methods typically represent candidate classes through learned output weights rather than directly matching visual evidence with textual class representations. To address the annotation gap, we present RA-GAR, a large-scale, richly annotated multimodal benchmark for gait attribute recognition, containing 1,001 subjects, 242,729 walking sequences, and annotations for 15 static and motion gait attributes. We further propose Gait-VL, an attribute-centric vision-language alignment framework that recognizes gait attributes by matching attribute-specific multi-frame visual evidence with textual class prototypes. On the visual side, attribute-specific learnable queries aggregate RGB features across spatial locations and frames into per-attribute visual embeddings. On the language side, diverse descriptions expanded by a large language model are combined with context about relevant body regions to construct textual class prototypes. Beyond attribute recognition, we evaluate the transferability of the attribute-pretrained visual encoder by using it to replace generic upstream large vision models in identityoriented gait recognition pipelines; attribute pre-training uses no identity classification or metric-learning objectives. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art attribute recognition performance on RA-GAR and consistent improvements in downstream identity recognition across multiple pipelines and benchmarks, supporting the effectiveness and transferability of attribute-centric gait representation learning.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] ToF-Wheel Odometry: Navigating Degeneration of Localization With Limited Sensing Capabilities
item.description: arXiv:2610.14590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wheel odometry provides an efficient motion prior for ground robots but is prone to transient violations such as wheel slip or terrain-induced tilt. In filtering-based odometry, these violations frequently trigger divergence when they coincide with constrained geometric observability (e.g., featureless corridors). We address this challenge by proposing ToF-Wheel Odometry (TWO), a tightly-coupled filtering framework that integrates wheel kinematics with geometric constraints from Time-of-Flight (ToF) cameras. The primary contribution of this work is a degeneracy-aware, directional covariance-shaping strategy that replaces heuristic online covariance tuning with geometry-conditioned inflation. The core idea is to infer process noise from geometric corrections with a strict reliability check. We decompose the posterior-to-prior correction into a wheel-explainable subspace and an orthogonal remainder. The process covariance is anisotropically adjusted according to the observability of the ToF update: if the geometry is degenerate in non-kinematic directions, the remainder is suppressed as sensor noise; if the geometry is distinct, it is admitted as a valid kinematic violation. Additionally, we introduce an intra-frame feedback loop that retrospectively repairs the process covariance within the current frame to reduce structural lag during bursty disturbances. Extensive experiments on challenging scenarios demonstrate that TWO improves trajectory accuracy and robustness compared to static and adaptive Gaussian filtering, robustly navigating the trade-off between kinematic reliability and limited sensing capabilities.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] SpikCTU: A Compact Spiking Network with Adaptive Recurrent Computation for Speech Command Recognition
item.description: arXiv:2610.14594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks offer event-driven, energy-efficient computation for speech command recognition, yet most existing methods follow fixed computation paths, allocating redundant computation to easy samples while providing limited insight into how evidence evolves during inference. To address these challenges, we introduce SpikCTU, a compact spiking network with adaptive recurrent computation for speech command recognition. Specifically, a hybrid spiking embedding module preserves continuous input information alongside spike features to construct a fixed temporal memory. A shared Continuous Thinking Unit (CTU) repeatedly reads this memory using keys derived from spikes and continuous values, and updates a binary recurrent state with lightweight stage adapters. Furthermore, combining a fixed base prediction with accumulated corrections at each step enables learned aggregation over all steps or confidence-based early exit using only the predictions available so far. Experiments on three speech command recognition benchmarks show that SpikCTU achieves competitive accuracy with only 0.16--0.17M parameters, and the early exit strategy can substantially further reduce computational cost without compromising accuracy. In addition, trajectory and attention analyses reveal that recurrent steps enable error correction and progressively refine predictions. Code is available at https://github.com/Rivflyyy/spikctu.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Load-Aware Quadruped Navigation with Online Contact-based Geometry Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2610.14596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Navigating cluttered environments while carrying objects remains a challenging problem for quadruped robots. Compared with works that focused on load-aware locomotion adaptation to maintain gait stability, existing autonomous navigation systems generally ignore the influence of carried objects' geometries and use fixed footprint inflation, leading to overly conservative navigation. To fill this knowledge gap, we propose a two-phase load-aware navigation learning framework. In Phase 1, we train LOADNav, a load-aware navigation policy via reinforcement learning, enabling the robot to adapt its trajectory and clearance behavior according to the geometric size of the carried object. In Phase 2, we train CoGE, an online geometry predictor via imitation learning, which estimates unknown payload geometry from occasional contact events. We evaluate the framework in cluttered environments with loads of varying sizes and shapes. The results show that our navigation policy exhibits clear load-aware behaviors, and the online geometry predictor estimates object geometry from occasional contact events, refining its estimate and adapting the navigation behavior accordingly. Without requiring any prior knowledge of the payload, it narrows the gap to geometry-aware policies.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Bidirectional Adaptive Transformers for Multimodal Anomaly Detection
item.description: arXiv:2610.14598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effective integration of features derived from RGB images and 3D point clouds presents a substantial challenge in the field of multimodal anomaly detection (MAD). Existing MAD methods typically rely on static fusion paradigms built upon frozen pre-trained encoders. While these frameworks facilitate spatial alignment, they lack the mechanism to establish latent semantic correspondence, thereby inducing cross-modal interference that degrades anomaly discriminability. To mitigate these limitations, this study proposes a Bidirectional Adaptive Transformers (BAT) framework, which constructs comprehensive and semantically aligned multimodal representations by leveraging complementary attributes across modalities. The BAT framework introduces a Bidirectional Feature Alignment (BFA) module, which employs a mutual predictive mechanism to bridge the gap between 2D textural patterns and 3D geometric structures. This bidirectional interaction explicitly enhances the textural granularity of point cloud descriptors while augmenting the spatial contextual awareness of RGB features. To ensure that the latent representations possess sufficient informational density for alignment, BAT incorporates a parameter-efficient adaptation architecture. By utilizing lightweight image and point cloud adapters, the framework facilitates specialized fine-tuning of pre-trained models, mitigating the information loss inherent in frozen encoders. Extensive experiments conducted on MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies confirm that BAT achieves state-of-the-art anomaly detection performance, significantly outperforming existing MAD methods.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] A new convergence proof for an iterative scheme for elliptic Cauchy problems based on alternating orthogonal projections
item.description: arXiv:2610.14600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an elliptic Cauchy problem for the Poisson equation in which both Dirichlet and Neumann boundary data are prescribed only on a portion of the boundary, while no boundary conditions are available on the remaining part of the boundary. Such problems are severely ill-posed. In this work, we study the convergence of an iterative method based on the alternating imposition of Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. We formulate the scheme within a Hilbert space framework, where a yet another alternation becomes apparent: each iteration can now be interpreted as an orthogonal projection onto an appropriate closed subspace. This perspective provides a transparent geometric interpretation of the algorithm and yields a concise convergence proof based on von Neumann's classical result on alternating (orthogonal) projections. In addition to elucidating the convergence of the method, this alternating projections perspective also offers a general rate of convergence in terms of the Friedrichs angle (between two closed subspaces). We point out by means of an example that such convergence rate estimate degenerates for the elliptic Cauchy problem under consideration.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] StateSkill-Agent: An Effective and Efficient Embodied Agent via State-conditioned Skill
item.description: arXiv:2610.14601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we aim to develop an embodied MLLM agent that understands and solves embodied tasks by learning, abstracting, and reusing transferrable and generalizable behavioral patterns. To this end, we propose StateSkill, a new skill representation for embodied agents, which introduces the concept of "finite-state machines" into skill modeling for effective and efficient skill construction and learning. The core idea of StateSkill is to model embodied interaction experiences as a finite-state machine, where a skill is organized around a set of task-progress states, state transitions, and state-conditioned guidance, enabling embodied agents to dynamically adjust their skills as the task progresses while keeping skill contexts compact and stage-relevant. We further develop StateSkill-Evolve, an experience-driven evolution mechanism that iteratively refines StateSkill through retrospective analysis of new successful and failed state-guided trajectories. Upon this, we introduce StateGRPO, which integrates StateSkill evolution and model optimization via state-conditioned GRPO into a unified iterative learning loop, enabling state-conditioned skills and model capabilities to co-evolve and reinforce each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods and trained model (i.e., StateSkill-Agent) across various embodied tasks.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] AnyRank: Reliable Anytime Policy Ranking via Sequential Testing
item.description: arXiv:2610.14603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Due to the high cost of hardware experiments, robot policies are predominantly evaluated by comparing their empirical performance on a limited number of hardware trials. However, finite-sample statistical uncertainty can lead to erroneous conclusions, especially when ranking multiple policies using a fixed batch of evaluation data. We propose AnyRank: a sequential method for multi-policy ranking that (i) adaptively allocates trials to hard-to-separate policies, (ii) provides (partial) rankings at any stopping time while bounding the probability of an incorrect ranking, and (iii) optionally exploits prior information to prioritize hardware evaluations more efficiently. This prior information could be informed from expert intuition, a small set of held-out hardware evaluations, or from policy rollouts in a simulator or an action-conditioned video world model. Notably, the prior can be imperfect; while a strong prior can provide efficiency gains on hardware, any inaccuracies in prior policy rankings do not invalidate the statistical assurances of AnyRank. We achieve the aforementioned properties through novel theoretical contributions that combine sequential testing with multiple-hypothesis graphical testing approaches. Experiments in simulation and real-world policy evaluation benchmarks show that AnyRank requires up to 50% fewer hardware evaluations compared to existing statistically rigorous approaches, while guarding against the incorrect rankings produced by heuristic methods used by state-of-the-art benchmarks.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] The Matching Number Characterizes the Query Complexity of Edge Counting and Degree Moment Estimation
item.description:
arXiv:2610.14604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider an unknown graph $G = (V,E)$ with vertex degrees $d_v$, accessed only by sampling uniformly random edges and querying the degrees of their endpoints. We study the query complexity of estimating the number of edges $m$ and the degree moments $M_s = \sum_{v \in V} (d_v)^s$ for fixed integers $s \ge 2$. In this model, [Beretta and T\v{e}tek, TALG 2024] estimate $m$ within relative error $\varepsilon$ using $O(\log n/\varepsilon^2+\sqrt n/\varepsilon)$ expected queries without knowing the number of vertices $n$, and [Bhattacharya and Pradhan, CIAC 2025] estimate $M_s$ using $O(n^{1-1/s}/\varepsilon^2)$ queries when $n$ is given. We show that the query complexity of both problems is governed by the matching number $
u$ of $G$ (the maximum number of pairwise disjoint edges) rather than the number of vertices $n$, and that the dependence on $\varepsilon$ for degree moments can be polynomially improved. Our algorithms rest on a simple observation: the endpoints of a maximum matching cover every edge, so a random endpoint of a random edge falls on this set of $2
u$ vertices with probability at least $1/2$. For every $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, we give advice-free algorithms that estimate $m$ and $M_s$ within relative error $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$, without knowledge of $n$, $
u$, or other graph parameters. Specifically, our algorithms use $O(\min\{
u/\varepsilon, 1/\varepsilon^2+\sqrt
u/\varepsilon\})$ expected queries for $m$ and $O(\min\{
u^{1-1/s}/\varepsilon^{2/s}, 
u^{1-1/(2s-1)}/\varepsilon^{2/(2s-1)}\})$ for $M_s$. Finally, our lower bounds show that for every $k \ge 2$ and sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, these query complexities are optimal up to constant factors over graphs with matching number at most $k$.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Decoupling Knowledge Forgetting and Refusal Learning in MLLM Unlearning
item.description: arXiv:2610.14605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current evaluations of multimodal unlearning typically focus on whether a model stops outputting target information. This surface-level criterion, however, masks two critical failure modes. First, knowledge suppression techniques often induce confabulation, leading the model to hallucinate facts about the unlearned subject. Second, refusal training merely alters observable behavior without erasing the underlying knowledge; such models might decline open queries but still identify correct answers under multiple-choice probing. To overcome these limitations, we propose Forget-Aware Self-Distillation (FASD). This method is designed to achieve honest ignorance, a state where the model genuinely loses the target knowledge and learns to acknowledge its absence. FASD separates these goals into two complementary channels. The behavior channel distills appropriate refusals from an ignorance-prompted copy of the model itself. Crucially, target tokens are masked from the teacher distribution to avoid accidentally reteaching the forgotten concepts. Simultaneously, the knowledge channel directly suppresses ground-truth answer spans independently of the model's generated responses. Experiments demonstrate that FASD successfully unlearns target knowledge, prevents information leakage in open-ended tasks, and preserves performance on retained data. The resulting model not only forgets the specified information but accurately recognizes the boundaries of its own knowledge. Code and data will be released upon publication.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Decision Uncertainty-Oriented Watermarking (DUOW): Securing Multi-Agent Routing Against Policy Cloning
item.description: arXiv:2610.14606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routing policies in Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) represent valuable intellectual property, yet their exposure through execution logs creates significant risks of unauthorized policy cloning. Existing agent watermarking methods protect intellectual property by modifying internal generation processes, such as perturbing token sampling distributions or injecting structural mutations into action trajectories, which may compromise task fidelity or suffer from limited transferability across heterogeneous platforms. To address these limitations, we propose Decision Uncertainty-Oriented Watermarking (DUOW), a lightweight framework that operates at the external decision layer without modifying model parameters or generated outputs. DUOW introduces a plug-and-play scoring mechanism that evaluates candidate agents from semantic and operational perspectives, identifies functionally redundant routing decisions, and selectively redirects choices among equivalent alternatives to embed ownership signals. By coupling watermark behaviors with utility-preserving routing decisions, DUOW enables cloned policies to retain ownership signals during policy imitation while increasing the difficulty of watermark removal. A confidence-driven adaptive threshold dynamically determines embedding opportunities, balancing watermark capacity and task fidelity under diverse routing contexts. Extensive evaluations on four multi-agent routing benchmarks demonstrate that DUOW preserves high task utility, achieves reliable ownership verification under up to 90% log erasure, and introduces negligible computational overhead, with an average per-step latency of 0.043 ms and total embedding overhead below 0.54 ms.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Window Size Matters: Benchmarking Voice Activity Detectors in Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.14607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Voice activity detection (VAD) sits in front of almost every streaming speech recognizer, yet the choice of detector is often made by feel rather than by measurement. We report a frame-level offline benchmark of three detectors on the test-clean split of LibriVAD-small: the neural TEN VAD, the neural Silero VAD and a simple RMS energy baseline. The evaluation covers 2,214 noisy utterances (about 7.1 hours) built from LibriSpeech, nine noise families and six SNR levels from -5 to 20 dB. At a 16 ms hop, TEN VAD reaches a ROC AUC of 0.917, an average precision of 0.968 and an F1 of 0.913. A sweep over 20, 30, 40 and 50 ms windows shows TEN to be almost insensitive to frame length (AUC 0.916 to 0.919), while RMS stays near 0.75 to 0.77. Silero matches TEN only near its native 32 ms input size and drops to 0.63 at 20 ms. We hypothesize that this is likely caused by our fixed-frame protocol rather than by the model itself. Zero padding, sub-chunk averaging and unreset model state are the likely factors, but we have not ablated them. In a per-condition breakdown of TEN, babble noise at low SNR stays close to chance. We also show that F1 at a fixed 0.5 threshold is a weak metric on this data, because a trivial all-speech detector already scores 0.854. All settings needed to reproduce the results are given in the paper.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] EviScene: Beyond "Is It AI?" for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment
item.description: arXiv:2610.14609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining whether an image is AI-generated does not establish whether the situation it depicts is factually supported. We formulate Image Factuality Assessment: given an image and a generic verification instruction, a system returns a supported or refuted verdict with an evidence-grounded explanation. Without a supplied textual claim, the system must progressively refine factual questions during investigation and align external evidence with the specific situation depicted. We introduce EviLens, an expert-reviewed benchmark of 10,174 supported and refuted images from controlled construction and web collection, covering twelve factual error types and evaluating both verdict accuracy and evidence sufficiency. We develop EviScene, a multimodal ReAct agent that interleaves visual inspection, external retrieval, and evidence analysis, using new findings to refine its questions and revisit relevant image details. We train a compact policy with supervised fine-tuning on reviewed teacher trajectories, followed by privileged on-policy self-distillation applied to verified decisions from the policy's own investigations. On the 1,527-image test set, the trained Qwen3.5-9B agent achieves 79.05% balanced accuracy and a Strict Evidence Sufficiency Rate (SESR) of 52.26%, improving over the same-backbone base agent by 6.71 and 9.37 percentage points, respectively. Its SESR is the highest among the evaluated agents.Code, models, and data will be released at https://github.com/wangzian828/EVISCENE and https://huggingface.co/ZiAnwang/EviScene.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] LLM-Augmented Bayesian Optimization with Adaptive Policies for Chiplet Design Space Exploration
item.description: arXiv:2610.14612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiplet technology is a key approach for extending Moore's Law. However, its design process is constrained by two primary challenges: the scarcity of early-stage platforms for rapidly evaluating chiplet-based heterogeneous systems, and the complex relationships between design parameters and optimization metrics. To address these challenges, we propose a synergistic framework that integrates a Large Language Model (LLM) with Bayesian Optimization (BO), enabling architectural-level simulation and automated optimization for the 2.5D/3D CPU-GPU heterogeneous chiplets. We extend the open-source chiplet simulator to evaluate 3D designs by supporting graph topologies. Further, to enhance the exploration efficiency of BO, we introduce an LLM that generates high-quality policies to guide the optimization process, enabled by our proposed adaptive directional policy reasoning (ADPR) and an exploration gain-aware fine-tuning method. Finally, we use the policy-guided BO to perform an automated and efficient exploration of the complex chiplet design space. Experiments on 2.5D and 3D chiplet reveal that our framework improves design space exploration efficiency.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Limitations on Autoregressive Token Generation via Sequential Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.14615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study autoregressive token generation through the notion of sequential samplers: A circuit that samples the next symbol only given the previous ones and possibly a small amount of state. We show that (1) a sequential sampler with $k$ bits of state can be simulated by a stateless one at a roughly $O(2^{k})$ size overhead; (2) efficient insertional sampling (Stern, Chan, Kiros, Uszkoreit, ICML 2019) is more powerful than efficient sequential sampling in any fixed order; (3) sequential samplers with small state cannot establish certain forms of covert cryptographic channels. Result (1), together with the pseudoentropy vs. sequential sampleability duality of Vadhan and Zheng (STOC 2012), characterizes efficient sequential sampleability with small state. Result (3) provides a potential safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Shifted-Chart Composition for Horizon-Optimal Time-Varying LQR
item.description: arXiv:2610.14621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Horizon optimization in finite-horizon LQR treats the horizon $T$ as a decision variable and adds a penalty $wT$ to the cost. Recent composition-based methods evaluate all candidate horizons in $O(Nn^3)$, instead of the $O(N^2n^3)$ of one Riccati recursion per horizon, but they track the inverse cost-to-go $P^{-1}$ and therefore require every stage and terminal cost to be positive definite, whereas LQR requires only positive semidefiniteness. This excludes costs that leave some states unpenalized. In this work, we track instead the shifted inverse $\widehat{P}_k=(P_k+cI)^{-1}$, the inverse coordinate after a symplectic shear of the state-costate variables. Its domain contains every positive semidefinite Riccati matrix, and $P_k=\widehat{P}_k^{-1}-cI$ recovers the Riccati solution. We show that the shift can be absorbed into the stage coefficients of the inverse-coordinate composition, so the $O(Nn^3)$ search carries over, exact in exact arithmetic, subject to invertibility conditions. These hold for all small $c$ when the dynamics contract the unpenalized directions, fail for at most finitely many $c$ outside a degenerate case, and are certified per horizon at run time. In our experiments, diagonal loading $Q_k+\varepsilon I$ either left cost errors several orders of magnitude above those of the shifted chart or, for small fixed $\varepsilon$, selected the wrong horizon. The shifted chart with a fixed default $c$ selected the correct horizon on all tested instances, reporting long horizons as uncertified in one stress case.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] From Rainfall to Road-Network Functionality: Transferable Graph Forecasting for Flood-Disrupted Transportation Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.14622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme rainfall can rapidly degrade road-network functionality (RNF), disrupting emergency mobility, accessibility, evacuation, logistics, and infrastructure restoration. Existing flood-transportation impact models are often difficult to deploy across regions because they rely on local calibration, intensive simulation workflows or target-region retraining. This study proposes G-R2R, a transferable spatiotemporal graph-learning framework that reframes rainfall-induced road-network disruption as a region-conditioned, topology-flexible graph forecasting problem for unseen transportation networks. The framework integrates ego-centered subgraph sampling, terrain-conditioned graph representation, region-conditioned dual-level static encoding, and dynamic rainfall-network feature learning. Static geographic and infrastructure attributes are fused with rainfall forcing and recent RNF states to forecast node-level RNF across heterogeneous road networks. G-R2R is evaluated using simulation-derived RNF sequences from ten flood-prone regions in Wenzhou, China, under unseen-region testing protocols. It outperforms representative forecasting baselines, achieving a stabilized MAPE of 2.33% and $R^2$ of 0.855 under the fixed unseen-region benchmark. Leave-one-area-out evaluation yields stabilized MAPE values of 2.30%-3.54%. Ablation analysis supports the contributions of the terrain-conditioned graph representation and dual-level static encoding. A historical-event replay of Typhoon Fitow further shows that G-R2R reproduces principal temporal trajectories and node-level spatial patterns of the simulation-derived RNF reference under observed rainfall forcing without target-region retraining. These results support rapid and transferable node-level RNF forecasting across the regional road-network domains represented in this study.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] EarthAlign: Learning Language-Aligned Representations of Earth System Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.14624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interpreting Earth system conditions is central to understanding environmental risks and informing decisions across weather- and climate-sensitive sectors. Existing multimodal weather systems primarily target task-specific prediction, generation, or question answering, while general-purpose alignment between Earth system data and language remains underexplored due to the limited availability of diverse language supervision grounded in meteorological conditions. To fill this gap, we introduce EarthAlign, a large-scale dataset with broad geographic coverage spanning 2000-2024 that combines 10 expert-curated natural event and disaster data sources with climatology-derived normal-weather samples. Each sample includes temporal and geospatial information and four grounded caption styles aligned with 63-variable ERA5 meteorological data. Building on EarthAlign, we introduce MeteoLIP, a dual-encoder framework for learning aligned meteorology-language representations. MeteoLIP incorporates MetTok, which uses a geolocation- and time-conditioned query to aggregate variable-specific patch embeddings into a compact sequence of meteorology tokens. To comprehensively assess Earth system multimodal representations, we introduce three downstream tasks: cross-modal retrieval, weather-condition classification, and physical variable estimation. Our experiments show that MeteoLIP improves upon the corresponding CLIP and SigLIP baselines across these tasks. Further analyses highlight the importance of meteorological input, temporal and geospatial conditioning, and multi-style supervision for meteorology-language alignment. Thus, EarthAlign and MeteoLIP provide a foundation for learning and evaluating language-aligned representations of Earth system data. Our code, dataset, and weights are publicly available at https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/EarthAlign.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] From Existing Methods to New Research Ideas: Two Perspectives on Recursive Self-Improvement
item.description: arXiv:2610.14625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a route to AI systems that participate in their own continued development. Recent methods allow language agents to retain changes to their parameters, memory, skills, and code for subsequent execution and improvement. We examine how these methods can inform new research ideas through two complementary perspectives. First, we introduce a unified taxonomy with nine design dimensions organized into four groups: update targets, update organization, update schedule and scope, feedback and selection. This taxonomy places existing methods in a shared design space, where examining individual dimensions and their interactions can inspire new research ideas. Second, we examine how existing RSI methods draw on traditional deep learning, for example through optimization, regularization, data augmentation, continual learning, and adversarial learning. We develop further ideas by examining more specific learning mechanisms and drawing on evolutionary computation. We also review how existing benchmarks assess self-improvement under online, offline, and offline-to-online settings. Together, these perspectives help researchers develop new RSI research ideas from existing designs and learning mechanisms. RSI papers and resources are available at https://prism-shadow.github.io/awesome-rsi/.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] TagBO: LLM-Driven Task-Aware Graph Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Discovery
item.description: arXiv:2610.14626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-variable optimization in scientific discovery often requires exploring large combinatorial spaces under costly experimental evaluations, making sample?efficient Bayesian optimization (BO) essential. However, existing BO methods typ?ically rely on structural descriptors to define similarity among categorical variables, implicitly assuming that structural similarity reflects similarity in task performance. In scientific optimization, this assumption is often violated, leading to surrogate representations that are poorly aligned with the optimization objective. To address this limitation, we propose TagBO (Task-aware Graph Bayesian Optimization), a method that integrates LLM-derived relational priors with descriptor-based struc?tural information for mixed-variable Bayesian optimization. Rather than directly using LLM outputs as predictive scores, TagBO treats LLM outputs as a potentially noisy source of task-aware relational priors and extracts coarse ordinal relational signals from LLM reasoning to construct task-aware similarity structures for scien?tific optimization. TagBO then performs constrained Gaussian process Bayesian optimization over the resulting joint discrete-continuous representation space. Ex?periments on diverse chemistry and materials formulation tasks demonstrate that TagBO consistently improves sample efficiency under fixed evaluation budgets across LLMs of varying capabilities.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Executable but Unfaithful: Mock Object, Stub, and Assertion Generation by LLMs and Coding Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.14629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mocking is a foundational practice in unit testing, enabling developers to isolate the code under test by replacing real dependencies with simulated alternatives. Automating the generation of mock objects, stubs, and mock assertions has been a long-standing research goal. However, capture-and-replay approaches rely on recording the runtime behavior of actual dependencies. Evolutionary approaches such as StubCoder overcome this requirement but constrain generation to predefined symbol pools. Large language models (LLMs) and coding agents offer an alternative by generating mocking artifacts from source code without requiring recorded dependency executions or fixed symbol pools. Yet, no systematic study has evaluated their capabilities across all three artifact types. To address this gap, we construct MockBench, a benchmark comprising 165 mock artifact generation tasks from real-world Java and Python projects, with validated reference mock objects, stubs, and mock assertions. We evaluate six LLMs and three coding agents in terms of executability, behavior fidelity, and interaction-fault detection capability, complemented by comparisons with existing tools and sensitivity analysis. Experimental results show that LLMs and coding agents indeed have been the state-of-the-art techniques in mock-based testing. More specifically, compared with LLMs, coding agents substantially improve executability, while these gains do not consistently translate into higher behavior fidelity or better interaction-fault detection. Furthermore, we analyze 660 failures from LLMs and coding agents, and identify ten error types across the three artifact categories, revealing behavioral deviations that passing tests can conceal. Our findings highlight the challenges of mock artifact generation and provide practical guidance for both developers and researchers.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] DuSRFlow: Dual-Lens Super-Resolution via Parallax-Aware Flow Estimation and Complementary Reference Warping
item.description: arXiv:2610.14630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dual-lens super-resolution (DuSR) aims to enhance a wide-angle low-resolution (LR) image by exploiting a telephoto reference (Ref) image. A central challenge in DuSR is reliable reference utilization under large parallax, occlusion, and cross-camera imaging discrepancies. Existing methods often employ off-the-shelf monocular optical flow models to provide geometric priors. However, their assumptions of photometric consistency and smooth motion are violated in dual-lens scenarios, leading to unreliable alignment and degraded reference-based reconstruction. To address these issues, we propose DuSRFlow, a dual-lens super-resolution framework that improves reference utilization from both correspondence learning and reference aggregation. First, we introduce DuFlowNet, a dedicated dual-lens flow estimator for robust cross-view alignment. To train DuFlowNet without ground-truth flow annotations, we develop a real--synthetic data fusion strategy that composites synthetic foreground objects onto real dual-lens image pairs, generating controllable large-parallax samples while preserving realistic cross-camera imaging characteristics. Second, we observe that reference reliability is highly spatially uneven in DuSR, where unreliable local reference responses may suppress the utilization of reliable cues. We therefore propose a Complementary Reference Warping strategy that coordinates patch-based warping and kernel-free-guided deformable warping according to local reference reliability, producing a more reliable reference representation before LR--Ref fusion. In addition, we construct DuSR-RealV2, a challenging real-world benchmark with complex depth variations, large parallax, and occlusion. Extensive experiments on multiple DuSR benchmarks demonstrate that DuSRFlow achieves state-of-the-art performance in reconstruction quality, perceptual quality, and cross-dataset generalization.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Automatic assembly modeling through attention-based assembly feature mate prediction and assembly feature pattern recognition
item.description: arXiv:2610.14633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assembly modeling plays an important role in constructing product models, yet it is still mainly performed via interactive operations that are experience-dependent and labor-intensive. Data-driven strategies hold promise for automating this process; however, existing approaches either predict poses that cannot directly generate editable B-Rep assembly constraints or require prescribed part pairs or predefined assembly faces. To reduce the large candidate space of constraint prediction without predefined assembly faces, we propose a data-driven framework based on assembly feature mate prediction. The framework performs automatic assembly modeling from unassembled B-Rep parts, using assembly features to group the geometric entities of local mating interfaces and restrict candidate formation. Given the lack of suitable assembly feature annotations in existing datasets, we construct a large-scale dataset through an automatic annotation pipeline. Using the annotated dataset, we train an attention-based network to predict assembly feature mates, with Engineering Compatibility Fusion (ECF) incorporating explicit engineering compatibility into learned matching scores. To improve the accuracy of automatic assembly modeling, we use assembly feature patterns (AFPs) to guide the matching process. Finally, a post-processing search selects assembly feature mate and AFP mate candidates, whose associated constraints are generated and solved to complete assembly modeling. Experimental results show that the framework achieves assembly constraint accuracies of 74.79% on the six-assembly comparison set and 64.09% on the extended test set of 16 assemblies, which includes the comparison set. With ground-truth face labels supplied as additional input, the corresponding accuracies increase to 81.78% and 80.93%, respectively.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] VbotNav-0: Asynchronous Cloud-Edge Dual-Policy Navigation across Indoor and Outdoor Environments
item.description: arXiv:2610.14634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous indoor-outdoor navigation connects destination-level reasoning with motion decisions that must respond to current observations. We present VbotNav-0, a cloud-edge dual-policy framework that links these processes through asynchronous policy-to-policy conditioning. The cloud policy produces subgoal guidance from visual history, navigation instructions, and route tokens; the edge policy combines available guidance with current RGB and LiDAR observations to generate local trajectories. This formulation allows the local perception-action loop to continue between cloud updates. A common route representation connects indoor paths and outdoor map routes, and the training recipe combines navigation demonstrations, corrective data, and grounded visual question answering (VQA). In the reported closed-loop evaluation of 258 episodes across 145 scenes, VbotNav-0 achieves 55.04% success rate and 55.03% success weighted by path length.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] PVFH-Bench: Benchmarking Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.14635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have achieved remarkable progress across a wide range of multimodal tasks. However, object hallucination remains a persistent challenge, undermining model reliability in applications such as visual question answering, embodied agents, and human-AI decision support systems. In this paper, inspired by cognitive science studies on perceptual bias, we investigate a new failure mode termed Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination (PVFH). Specifically, PVFH refers to a premise-induced reasoning error in which models become anchored to visually confusable evidence, accept a false textual premise, and subsequently generate responses about an absent yet visually plausible object. To systematically study this phenomenon, we introduce PVFH-Bench, a benchmark that automatically constructs visually confusable but absent targets and pairs the core hallucination setting with diagnostic subsets to trace how models move from object recognition to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Experimental results on 10 state-of-the-art LVLMs demonstrate that all evaluated models are highly vulnerable to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Moreover, we find that explicit chain-of-thought reasoning can further exacerbate this failure mode by encouraging models to overinterpret weak visual cues as supporting evidence for hallucinated objects.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] PEARL: Process-Experience Aware Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.14636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Terminal rewards make multi-turn agents trainable without step-level annotations, but group-relative advantages provide little guidance about which intermediate decisions to adjust. Failed trajectories also contain reasonable actions, while unfavorable decision patterns can recur as training proceeds. We introduce PEARL (Process-Experience Aware Reinforcement Learning), which improves local credit assignment without an additional critic. Given two continuations from the same history with different outcomes, PEARL locates their first divergence and builds a feature representation of each branch's local decision. It clusters these decision features in recent failure and success memories to identify recurring local patterns. Using this pattern memory, PEARL selectively strengthens negative advantages at lower-reward decisions, while leaving positive advantages and the base policy optimizer unchanged. On AppWorld, PEARL improves over ARPO on Normal and Challenge tasks at both 4B and 8B scales. On ALFWorld, it achieves 97.9% mean success at 4B, 2.7 points above the strongest baseline, while remaining competitive at 8B. Ablations of shaping location, success-bank filtering, and memory window support the value of selective, recurring-pattern-based updates.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Defending Consensus-Based Cooperative Sensing Against Conformity-Driven Byzantine Attacks in 6G UAV Swarm Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.14639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enabled six-generation (6G) networks, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms increasingly rely on consensus-based cooperative sensing: each node iteratively exchanges and fuses decisions with its neighbors to approach a global picture of the environment, supporting the high-reliability, low-latency inference demanded by mission-critical tasks. Yet this very mechanism of conformity becomes the lever of Byzantine attacks. By exploiting the update rule, malicious nodes manufacture a false consensus that lures honest nodes into drifting away from their true observations round after round, so that a normal node's actual error probability evolves dynamically and rises far above its intrinsic sensing error. Conventional fusion models, which assume node errors are fixed and independent, are therefore severely mismatched. This article argues for a different defensive perspective: instead of hunting for bad nodes, we seek to understand how good nodes turn bad, characterizing the inducement dynamics with evolutionary game theory and handing this law to the fusion center so that it can dynamically correct the true error level of normal nodes. Simulations show that the approach sustains near-perfect situational inference across a wide range of attack intensities and network sizes, while naturally supporting low latency decisions. We further discuss several open challenges on the path toward secure ISAC-6G swarm sensing.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Optimal Receive Design on the Observation Axis for RSMA Satellite-UAV Downlinks
item.description: arXiv:2610.14641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A receiver can change its observation state while the physical signal remains the same. In rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlinks, this distinction separates receive-beam design and phase-reference transport from the motion of the satellite--UAV line of sight. We formulate receive optimization within the physical--observation dual-axis (PODA) structure and obtain three complementary results. For a known line-of-sight response and positive-definite receiver-noise covariance, a noise-weighted matched combiner simultaneously maximizes every decoding SINR and the minimum user rate. Under directional uncertainty, the principal eigenvector of the conditional response covariance globally maximizes mean array gain; for a Gaussian directional model, an equal-amplitude receiver is optimized by steering towards the conditional mean. Mean rate requires a different objective. We prove that the RSMA common-rate water level is jointly concave in the users' receive gains and derive a semidefinite relaxation with a computable global upper bound. A feasible rank-one beam can therefore be compared directly with the optimum of the finite-scenario problem. We also derive a precision-weighted linear predictor that suppresses uncertain physical-velocity estimates after observation-frame transport. Paired dynamic simulations reduce direction-cosine RMSE by 51.29\% relative to unrestricted nine-point extrapolation. In a separate uncertainty experiment, direct rate optimization increases mean minimum spectral efficiency from 0.32425 to 0.41712 bit/s/Hz, an improvement of 28.64\%; the corresponding design objective is within $2.28\times10^{-4}$ bit/s/Hz of a global upper bound. The phase-transport equation fixes a coherent representative of each optimal beam without changing its gain.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] AegisVox: Factorized Privacy and Clinical Preservation for Long-Form Speech
item.description: arXiv:2610.14643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical speech reveals identity through both spoken identifiers and voice, yet its pauses, delivery, and speaker roles can also carry useful clinical evidence. Protecting that speech therefore requires more than preserving its words. We present AegisVox, a factorized framework that assigns consistent surrogate voices and edits identifier-bearing turns using document-consistent replacements. Across 390 public simulated or non-patient conversations totaling 63.6 hours, a matched comparison of two speech renderers separates replacement realization from retained identifiers, speaker linkage, and clinical preservation. Text-to-speech rendering realizes 535/601 planned replacements versus 453/601 for the codec-based speech editor. However, similar aggregate clinical preservation conceals more model-labeled contradictions, and conversation-wide speaker scores conceal greater edited-speech linkage under a score-direction sensitivity analysis. Fresh transcription of original audio provides a reference for interpreting the clinical measurement chain; an independent judge tests sensitivity to model-based assessment. Better replacement realization can therefore coexist with worse clinical or speaker-linkage measurements. AegisVox supports use-specific evaluation of those tradeoffs, not a guarantee of identifier removal or clinical safety.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Beyond Independent Values: Optimal Auctions with Correlated Valuations for LLM-Native Advertising
item.description: arXiv:2610.14646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversational assistants are becoming the place where people ask what to buy, and sponsored content is moving into their answers. Several advertisers then compete for one sponsored slot, and all of them read the same conversation, so their willingness to pay usually moves together. Existing auctions for LLM advertising treat these values as independent. We therefore present AffMyerson, an auction that captures this correlation and turns it into revenue. We model the advertisers' values given the conversation as a multivariate normal and turn the economic premise of positive dependence (affiliation) into a sign condition on the precision matrix. We design a neural parameterization whose every output satisfies it. We prove that every prior in this family yields a truthful, ex-post individually rational auction, so estimation error can cost revenue but never truthfulness. We derive the conditional virtual values in closed form. By the design of the prior, pricing an auction needs no matrix inversion and takes O(n^2) time, fast enough to run at query time. We also work out the log-normal family used in empirical ad-auction work. There we prove that the auction is truthful for every prior and revenue-optimal when the prior is correct, and that the virtual value is regular everywhere whenever the conditional spread is below a loose threshold, which our fitted priors stay well under. With LLM-agent bidders, AffMyerson earns 6.2% more than a second-price auction with a tuned reserve, 6.1% more than Ronen's lookahead auction with the same prior, and 9.2% more than Myerson's auction run as if values were independent. This gain is still 4.5% on real keyword search queries where willingness to pay is hard to read. The correlation comes from common demand. Agents that judge the conversation bid together and agents told to calculate do not. The gain from conditioning moves with the correlation.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Can Synthetic UAV Benchmarks Be Trusted? Real-Synthetic Validation for UAV Model Selection
item.description: arXiv:2610.14647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic UAV imagery can expand pre-deployment test evidence when task-specific Real data are scarce, but visual plausibility or semantic label alignment alone does not establish validity for model selection. We study when Synthetic evaluation preserves the model-selection conclusions obtained from Real UAV data through two complementary cases under fixed evaluation protocols. In a requirement-specific road-debris benchmark, four language-conditioned perception systems obtain lower absolute F1 on Synthetic data, yet the point-estimate ordering and top-ranked model are preserved; bootstrap analysis yields no supported pairwise reversal, and size-matched resampling preserves the top-model decision. In contrast, a closed-set stress test on a separately materialized business corpus, using four VisDrone-compatible detectors over eight empirically supported classes, changes the point-estimate top-ranked detector and reverses three of six pairwise point-estimate preference directions. A complementary audit of five UAV business scenarios further reveals substantial Real-Synthetic mismatch in class composition, object density, and target scale, including systematic under-representation of small targets. These results show that Synthetic UAV benchmark trust is conditional: semantic coverage is insufficient, and validity must be established empirically for the task, operating regime, and model panel of interest.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] TAG: Calibrating SAM3 for Universal Image Segmentation without Dense Supervision
item.description: arXiv:2610.14651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recent Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) extends powerful promptable segmentation from spatial cues to concepts, raising the prospect of a single foundation model for universal image segmentation. However, this promise often fails to translate into reliable performance on downstream segmentation tasks. In this work, we empirically identify concept recognition, rather than mask quality, as the primary bottleneck: SAM3 accurately delineates the objects it recognizes yet struggles to robustly determine which concepts are present. Driven by this, we present \textit{\underline{T}ext \underline{A}nchor re-\underline{G}rounding (\TAG{})}, a simple yet effective framework that rectifies the concept recognition of SAM3 on the target domain without dense annotations. Specifically, \TAG{} introduces an \textit{Anchor Residual Pathway} comprising image-conditioned, low-rank adapters to re-ground text anchors in the target distribution and modulate subsequent text-conditioned interactions. Guided solely by image-level category labels, \TAG{} jointly optimizes binary cross-entropy with \textit{Soft Boundary Ranking} objectives to calibrate presence confidence and distinguish present concepts from confusable negatives. Building upon this, we devise \textit{Confidence-Weighted Distillation} to couple rich semantic context of a multimodal large language model with fine-grained spatial priors of SAM3, thereby achieving effective calibration in the absence of manual annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \TAG{} unlocks SAM3's segmentation potential with only 3.1M trainable parameters, achieving impressive performance across diverse scenarios, and notably, even surpassing leading mask-supervised methods on several metrics. \href{https://github.com/MiSsU-HH/TAG_SAM3}{Our code will be publicly available at GitHub \faGithub}.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Prospective Forcing: Learning to Look Ahead for Autoregressive Long Video Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.14654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autoregressive video generators synthesize long videos through chunk-wise rollouts, yet they are typically trained to predict only the immediate future. This limited prediction horizon makes it challenging to maintain video quality over extended rollouts. To address this problem, we introduce Prospective Forcing, a multi-head prediction framework that injects long-range predictive signals into autoregressive video representations. Built on a rolling-window generator, Prospective Forcing attaches lightweight, offset-specific heads that share the same conditioning information and independently predict chunks at different future temporal offsets. By extending supervision beyond the next chunk, these heads encourage the shared history representation to retain information useful for longer-horizon prediction, supporting temporally consistent generation. At inference time, we accelerate sampling by using accepted future-chunk predictions to skip full-window backbone executions. We equip the head with learnable embeddings to generate multiple candidates for the next chunk, and a learned verifier either selects a candidate or rejects all and falls back to standard autoregressive generation.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] TGuide: Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Historical Trajectory Guidance
item.description: arXiv:2610.14657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can autoregressive video diffusion be accelerated further when only four denoising steps remain? Existing feature caching approaches struggle in this regime, as large feature changes between denoising timesteps undermine both direct reuse and lightweight predictors. We observe that features across video chunks remain strongly correlated at matching denoising timesteps, offering a complementary source of guidance. Building on this insight, we introduce TGuide, a framework that accelerates autoregressive video diffusion through a lightweight Anchor-Transport-Correct (ATC) predictor guided by historical sampling trajectories. Our ATC combines two complementary references: the current chunk's preceding-step features preserve its spatial structure, while the previous chunk's same-timestep features provide information at the target denoising stage. By integrating these references through spatial retrieval and adaptive correction, ATC improves velocity prediction accuracy despite the large gaps between denoising steps. To mitigate error accumulation across both denoising steps and video chunks, we train the predictor on its own autoregressive rollouts, allowing it to adapt to states shaped by its own earlier predictions. An optional confidence-aware scheduler further adjusts the quality-efficiency trade-off. Experiments on Self Forcing, Causal Forcing, and HY-WorldPlay show that TGuide preserves generation quality while achieving denoising speedups of up to $1.89\times$ over the original 4-step generators. On Self Forcing, TGuide generalizes from 81-frame training videos to 333-frame generation, approximately four times the training length, while exceeding the original model's VBench score.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Learning Optimal Robust-Pathwise Control of Elliptic Equations with Random Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.14658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional control approaches to optimization problems under uncertainty entail a practical compromise: deterministic controls offer robustness at the expense of pathwise accuracy while stochastic controls can adapt to individual realizations but suffer from the curse of dimensionality. To achieve both robustness and adaptivity, a neural operator-based approach is proposed in this paper for distributed elliptic optimal control problems with high-dimensional random inputs. A data-driven training algorithm is first established to learn the mapping from coefficient realizations directly to their optimal pathwise controls. To bypass the burden of generating training data pairs, a physics-informed training algorithm is then proposed and recast as weakly supervised learning using pseudo label targets produced by standard adjoint-based control updates. Numerical experiments with rough coefficients are conducted to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our robust-pathwise controls, which outperforms the benchmark robust deterministic control on unseen coefficient realizations owing to the generalization capability and fast inference of trained models.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] RASSG: Repair-Aware Semantic Survival Gating for Streaming Tool Execution
item.description: arXiv:2610.14659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Streaming speech assistants can launch tools before users finish speaking, overlapping execution with incoming speech to reduce user waiting time. However, subsequent self-corrections can invalidate apparently stable arguments, causing stale execution whose irreversible effects persist even after the final call is corrected. We propose Repair-Aware Semantic Survival Gating (RASSG) to jointly control tool launch and cancellation during streaming speech. RASSG launches a tool when three consecutive speech recognition results arrive with identical nonempty arguments, then combines calibrated argument invalidity risk with execution costs to decide cancellation at the last feasible opportunity before effects become irreversible. Evaluation on ReCAST, FDB-v3, and Audio2Tool uses a controlled execution clock with fixed tool runtimes and cancellation parameters. On ReCAST's prospective-repair subset, RASSG reduces the stale execution rate from LocalAgreement-2's 50.00% to 3.15%, with a mean delay of 3.676s across successful trajectories. The stale reduction also holds against every early-execution baseline on both public speech datasets. Ablations with identical initial launches support active cancellation, showing the value of controlling ongoing calls before their effects become irreversible. Code and data are available at https://github.com/daijinhu/RASSG.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Impact of Expertise and Trust on AI-assisted Work
item.description: arXiv:2610.14660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents promise to extend what users can accomplish beyond their existing expertise, but they also raise the risk of producing plausible-looking work that users may struggle to evaluate. We ask how task-relevant expertise and trust in AI shape agent-assisted work. To isolate these factors, we conduct a think-aloud study in which 20 professionals with varying data-science expertise use the same agentic tool to complete the same data-science hiring assessment, used at a major U.S. company. We find that surface productivity can come at the expense of understanding: participants who delegated more completed more of the task, but were also more likely to produce invalid solutions. Experts more often resisted this tradeoff, sacrificing completion to decompose the task and scrutinize agent outputs. Our findings call for evaluating agentic assistance not only by how much it accomplishes, but by whether users remain able to evaluate the work they produce.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Declared but Unaccountable: Measuring the Seller-Identity Gap in Advertising Supply-Chain Transparency
item.description: arXiv:2610.14661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public advertising transparency relies on a minimum accountability condition: an account authorized by a publisher in ads.txt or app-ads.txt should appear in the applicable sellers.json registry. When an available registry omits the declared seller ID, the authorization remains visible and machine-readable, but its public verification path breaks. We call this failure the seller-identity gap. We measure the gap using 233.4 million normalized advertising-transparency records and an absent-only, coverage-aware evidence rule. A declaration enters the numerator only when the applicable registry is available and omits its seller ID; unavailable, malformed, confidential, and other non-evaluable states remain separate. The resulting row-level floor is 24.25% in a high-popularity, low-removal reference population and 30.71% among publishers associated with at least 100 copyright-removal requests, a 6.45 percentage-point increase. The gap then remains near one third at stricter cumulative thresholds. Standardizing the populations to common weights over 1,469 shared ad systems reduces the primary contrast to 4.65 points: about 72% remains within systems, while 28% forms a composition-associated residual. We connect these population estimates to recurring seller-account coordinates, byte-identical declaration configurations, and provenance-bearing case packets. We frame this declaration-centered investigative use of public advertising records as Ad Transparency Intelligence: it reconstructs declared supply-chain relationships, identifies where public verification stops, and prioritizes evidence for corroboration without equating correlation with attribution. Advertising transparency supports accountability and investigation only when visible authorizations remain publicly verifiable.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Does Failure Feedback Direct Agent Self-Modification?
item.description: arXiv:2610.14662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-improving agents use failure feedback to revise their code or instructions, but gains after selection do not establish target-specific repair or generalization. We measure directedness by comparing repair of a randomly selected target failure with repair of the parent's other failures. Across 145 eligible modifications in public Darwin G\"odel Machine logs, we find no detectable target-specific advantage. Controlled instruction-revision experiments with small open models show that relevant feedback can improve target repair. In a second study with a pre-specified analysis plan, target feedback raised repair by 20 percentage points for Qwen3-4B relative to matched same-category feedback; the 7-point increase for Phi-4-mini was not significant. Target repair did not reliably imply held-out improvement. Held-out gains were concentrated in settings with identifiable, repairable failure mechanisms, including planted errors and natural tool-interface failures. Benefits of edit localization and regression screening varied across settings, while eight-step revision loops and GEPA ended at similar mean held-out accuracy. Evaluations should report target repair, transfer to related failures, and held-out net change separately.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] TETRIS-4DGS: Efficient Post-Training Compression of 4D Gaussian Splatting
item.description: arXiv:2610.14663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) has emerged as a powerful dynamic scene representation, supporting real-time high quality rendering but suffers from prohibitive storage overhead. Existing methods typically attempt to solve this by treating compression as a per-scene optimization problem, limiting generalizability and applicability where low-latency compression is required. In this work, we leverage existing image and video codecs and propose a generalized post-training compression framework for 4DGS to address these issues. Specifically, we apply importance-based adaptive quantization to Gaussians according to their importance levels, effectively refining bitrate allocation while remaining fully compatible with existing codecs. To further improve compression efficiency, we utilize the statistical properties of 4DGS and propose motion- and importance-aware packing to reorganize attributes into codec-friendly 2D maps. Our approach can achieve over 40x compression rate in seconds while maintaining high quality, facilitating the practical deployment of 4DGS.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Stable and effective restarting of the SS--RR and SS--RRR methods for computing partial eigenpairs of Hermitian matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.14669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider stable and effective restarts of the SS--RR and SS--RRR methods for computing the eigenpairs of a large Hermitian matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with the $n_{ev}$ eigenvalues in a given interval. Taking the CJ--SS--RR and CJ--SS--RRR methods for instance, we prove that the commonly used restart scheme and its orthonormalized variant, named the natural restart schemes, are not numerically stable, thereby lowering attainable accuracy of approximate eigenpairs and missing some of the $n_{ev}$ desired eigenpairs. To cure these deficiencies, we propose a new restart scheme, called the combination restart, that takes the $n\times \ell$ starting matrix to be the product of the matrix, which consists of the selected $n_{ev}$ approximate eigenvectors, and an $n_{ev}\times \ell$ Gaussian random matrix. We prove the remarkable mathematical and numerical superiority of the combination restart over the natural restarts, then present a hybrid restart scheme that fully exploits the advantages of the natural restart and combination restart, and finally develop CJ--SS--RR and CJ--SS--RRR algorithms with the hybrid restart. Numerical experiments confirm that the new algorithms are numerically backward stable to the working precision and more efficient than the CJ--SS--RRR algorithm with the natural restart. The combination restart and hybrid restart schemes can be straightforwardly extended to the SS--RR and SS--RRR methods for general standard and generalized eigenvalue problems.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Ascent Conditions for Length-Normalized Single-Rollout Policy Updates
item.description: arXiv:2610.14670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dividing each trajectory's score contribution by its realized length can change the direction of a reward-centered policy update. In a finite trajectory model, we derive an exact ascent threshold for a three-outcome softmax policy and exhibit a binary-reward example in which the expected Euclidean update decreases task success. Natural-gradient ascent holds for fully controllable outcome distributions with deterministic binary labels, but can fail under a one-parameter restriction. A third-order U-statistic estimates the first-order return change without bias from independent current-policy trajectories, one per request. In the example, a same-sample plug-in estimator instead has the opposite sign in expectation for batch sizes two through forty-nine. Exact policy-grid enumeration confirms the local sign reversal. In a branching process, length-normalized learning initially loses return, then recovers and exceeds the unnormalized comparator. The analysis concerns the expected update field at the current policy.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] SPARE: Shared Perception and Adaptive Retrieval of Evidence for Streaming Video Understanding
item.description: arXiv:2610.14671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Streaming video understanding requires answering questions from the observed video, with evidence drawn from recent observations or earlier events. Historical context can improve recall but may interfere with judgments based on recent frames. Its usefulness depends on both when it is introduced and which clips are selected, while relevance alone does not guarantee sufficient evidence for an answer. We propose SPARE, a framework that combines adaptive historical retrieval with visual encoder sharing. A lightweight gate predicts whether recent observations provide sufficient evidence to answer the question. When additional evidence is predicted to be necessary, a multimodal embedding model retrieves relevant historical clips to supplement the current context. LoRA instruction tuning trains the understanding model to use recent observations and retrieved history jointly and abstain when the evidence remains insufficient. To reduce redundant visual parameters, the understanding and retrieval branches share a visual encoder while retaining separate language backbones. Four linear adapters align the shared features with the retrieval model through distillation at the visual token and final retrieval embedding levels. With visual-only inputs, SPARE achieves 77.78% on the evaluated Real-time and Backward task groups of OVO-Bench and 73.31% on StreamingBench. Compared with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluated at 2 fps, SPARE improves accuracy by 20.68 percentage points on OVO-Bench and 14.15 percentage points on StreamingBench.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Competition Domains Matter: Selective Head Globalization for Training-Free Sparse Attention in Video Diffusion Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2610.14672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training-free sparse attention is a practical route to efficient video diffusion transformer inference, yet existing methods typically fix the competition domain at each query row for every attention head. Prior work primarily addresses how to estimate token-level importance within this fixed domain; whether the domain itself should adapt to head heterogeneity remains under-specified. We introduce EG-Sparse, a training-free framework that routes low-entropy heads to a grouped cross-head pool while retaining per-row local selection for high-entropy heads, using only scores already materialized by the sparse pipeline. A controlled diagnostic fixes the ranking score and varies only the competition rule: grouped cross-head selection reduces low-entropy-head reconstruction error by 9.8%, whereas forcing high-entropy heads into an all-head global pool increases it by 7.9%. Across four configurations, EG-Sparse achieves higher video quality while reducing attention density and GPU denoising latency compared with strong training-free sparse-attention baselines. Mechanism ablations further show that selective domain adaptation outperforms uniform, random, and fixed domain-assignment policies. These results support competition-domain adaptation as a distinct design axis within centroid-guided training-free sparse attention.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] CAST-ASD: Causal Attention over Speakers and Time for Online Active Speaker Detection
item.description: arXiv:2610.14676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present CAST-ASD (Causal Attention over Speakers and Time), a causal joint model for active speaker detection (ASD). Recent ASD models improve performance by jointly processing all faces in a scene, but operate offline, with the full clip available before any frame is labelled. Low-latency causal detectors instead process each face independently. CAST-ASD combines joint face reasoning with fully causal inference. It applies scene-level attention across faces within the current frame and causal temporal attention over each face's history, enabling information sharing across speakers with zero lookahead. Its parameter count does not grow with the number of faces. On MSDWild, where most negative face-frames contain a visible competing speaker, CAST-ASD reduces competing-speaker false alarms by 32% relative to the causal per-face detector it extends, with larger gains as scene occupancy increases. It outperforms all causal baselines on both validation splits while using only one-tenth the inter-speaker parameters of a three-block fixed-roster convolution. Code and models are available at https://github.com/prathamg007/CAST-ASD.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] HADES: A Programmable Processing-Near-Memory Engine for Binary Similarity Search
item.description: arXiv:2610.14677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moving operands to a processor can cost more than the arithmetic performed on them, and for small binary similarity and search workloads data movement can dominate. We present HADES, a programmable processing-near-memory engine built around one shared 32x32-bit 2R1W register-file macro that holds both data and program.
