Tail recursion limits the interplay between fixpoints and higher-order functions so that model checking based on fixpoint iteration can be made more space efficient in a way comparable to tail recursion in programming languages. The capturing result makes use of a generalisation of Vardi's characterisation of PSPACE as first-order logic with partial fixpoints, namely that k-EXPSPACE is captured by higher-order logic of order k+1 with partial fixpoints.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Representation Theorems for Actual Powers over Two-Agent General Concurrent Game Frames
item.description: arXiv:2610.15476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the most well-known connections between logic and games is Pauly's representation theorem: the induced powers of individuals and coalitions in concurrent game frames correspond, in a precise sense, to a certain class of neighborhood frames. The precise sense here is what is called alpha effectivity (or alpha power): the power of a coalition is characterized by the sets of states in which it can ensure that the outcome lies by taking some joint action. This definition is inherently monotonic, and, as pointed out by van Benthem, Bezhanishvili, and Enqvist (2019), that fact can obscure relevant information about the power structure in the game: we do not know whether two sets that a coalition has the power to enforce correspond to the same joint action or to different joint actions. An alternative is to characterize the power of a coalition by its actual power (called basic power by van Benthem, Bezhanishvili, and Enqvist (2019)): the collection of sets of states, each of which corresponds to one joint action by the coalition and all possible joint actions by the other agents. It has recently been argued by Li and Ju (2025, 2026) that standard concurrent game frames rely on three assumptions that may, in some cases, be too strong: seriality, independence of agents, and determinism. This yields a total of eight different classes of general concurrent game frames. In this paper, assuming two agents, we prove that, in terms of actual powers, the eight classes of general concurrent game frames are represented by eight corresponding classes of neighborhood frames. This generalizes a result by van Benthem, Bezhanishvili, and Enqvist (2019).
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Whitney--Lagrange Decomposition for the First Family of Finite Element Differential Forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.15477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive polynomial bubble duality in barycentric coordinates and construct explicit nodal bases for the first family of finite element differential forms. Logarithmic coordinates give an elementary proof of the Whitney--bubble decomposition. The Hessian of negative entropy defines a metric whose normalized Hodge star maps bubble generators to complementary-degree polynomial forms. This gives a direct geometric description of the known dualities and proves nondegeneracy of their integral pairings. Combining Whitney forms with shifted Lagrange polynomials then gives bases dual to tangential point evaluations in every dimension and order. The construction extends to scalar nodes that are unisolvent on every face. The interpolant is independent of the roots and commutes with face restriction.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Execution-Time Opacity in (Controllable) Timed Automata is Hard
item.description: arXiv:2610.15478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Timing information leakage occurs whenever an attacker successfully deduces confidential internal information by observing some timed information such as the total duration of a run. Timed automata (TAs) are an extension of finite-state automata with a set of clocks evolving at the same rate and that can be tested or reset. Hence, this formalism is able to represent systems involving timing constraints reacting to the passage of time. Some of the transitions in a timed automaton may be controlled, i.e., enabled or disabled, to limit the runs that are allowed. Execution-time opacity (ET-opacity) aims at studying timing information leakage through the analysis of timed automata. More precisely, the ET-opacity problem consists in deciding whether an attacker can deduce whether some secret locations were visited by a run, solely from the run's duration. When control is allowed, the goal becomes to find a strategy that blocks the runs leaking information. This problem has been shown decidable for TAs, with and without control. However, these existing results only provide upper bounds on the complexity of the ET-opacity problem, sometimes largely above the tight bound. Our main contribution is to provide tight lower bounds for those two results. Moreover, for controllable TAs, two variants of ET-opacity (depending on whether detecting if a run did not visit a secret location represents an information leakage or not, and named full and weak ET-opacity respectively) had been separately studied; we prove here that these two notions are inter-reducible.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Lasso Games
item.description: arXiv:2610.15480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study games on finite graphs with labelled or weighted edges in which plays end as soon as the first loop is formed. The resulting play has a lasso shape: a path (head) followed by a cycle (loop). We consider two semantics for determining the winner: the loop semantics, where only the loop matters, and the lasso semantics, where the entire play is taken into account. We show that adopting the lasso semantics may have a dramatic impact on both the complexity of the game and the memory required to play optimally. Mean-payoff games with lasso semantics are no longer positionally determined, and the threshold problem â€“ deciding whether the value of the game is at least 0 â€“ is PSPACE-complete. In contrast, lasso parity games are equivalent to weak parity games, remain positionally determined and are solvable in polynomial time. Furthermore, we show that if a positionally determined winning objective is closed under cyclic permutation and both the objective and its complement are closed under concatenation, then it is equivalent to the parity objective. Finally, we consider mod-k games, where the winner depends on the length of the path modulo k >= 2. We show that these games, in both semantics, are PSPACE-complete. Alongside computational complexity, we analyze the memory required to play optimally. We establish that for any game positionally determined in loop semantics, memory of size 2^n is sufficient in lasso semantics. We complement this by showing exponential memory lower bounds for lasso mean-payoff and mod-k games.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] SkillFusion: Towards Reliable Multi-Skill Composition for LLM Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.15481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Independently authored skills can impose incompatible requirements, competing preferences, and redundant instructions when jointly loaded by an LLM agent. We propose SkillFusion, an offline compiler that reconciles these interactions into a reusable merged skill. Its central idea is to make composition decisions explicit through typed, scoped constraints linked to their source directives. A type-scope gate selects candidate interactions, while selective fallback revisits pairs potentially missed by structural pruning. A classifier identifies interaction types, and an adversarial verifier re-examines uncertain judgments. The resolver applies conditional routing or explicit priorities to hard conflicts, verified abstraction to soft conflicts, and deduplication to redundant instructions. Source-linked checks guide synthesis and compression, and metadata synthesis supports discovery of the merged skill. The resulting artifact retains associated scripts and resources and can be reused across tasks and executor models. SkillFusion achieves the highest mean Success among evaluated non-oracle methods on all three agent benchmarks and on both transfer benchmarks across three executor models. At the largest tested instruction configurations, it achieves over 2.5 times the Success of unresolved multi-skill loading, highlighting the growing value of reconciliation as composition becomes more demanding. The code will be open-sourced after the review process concludes.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Security in LLM-Assisted Coding: A Systematic Literature Review
item.description: arXiv:2610.15482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models accelerate software development but introduce severe security vulnerabilities. This systematic review investigates security risks in automated coding, benchmark limitations, and the role of human developers. Findings indicate that models frequently generate insecure code and faulty patches due to training data biases. Additionally, the models themselves are susceptible to direct attacks. Current evaluation methods suffer from data contamination and lack robust security metrics. Consequently, human oversight remains essential. Safer integration of automation will require more security-aware model architectures, stronger security-specific benchmarks, and more effective human-AI collaboration frameworks to mitigate these systemic risks.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Toward Explainability in Multimodal Recommendation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal recommender systems effectively alleviate data sparsity and cold-start problems by integrating heterogeneous information, yet complex cross-modal representations and model decision-making processes also introduce new interpretability challenges. Despite the rapid growth of research on the interpretability of multimodal recommendation in recent years, relevant methods and evaluation criteria remain relatively fragmented, lacking a unified conceptual framework. To address this gap, this paper categorizes existing methods into modality explanation and post-hoc explanation based on the timing and manner of explanation generation, and further constructs a progressive system for each category. Building on this foundation, this paper synthesizes four categories of evaluation metrics from both objective quantitative and subjective perceptual perspectives, and reviews relevant datasets along the dimensions of application domain and data source. Through a comprehensive analysis of existing research, we further propose future research directions. This paper aims to establish a unified analytical perspective across multimodal representation, recommendation decision-making, and user preferences, providing a research foundation for building transparent and trustworthy multimodal recommender systems.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Learning Safety-Constrained Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation for Lunar Surface Operations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robotic systems for lunar surface operations must act autonomously and preserve their own integrity in an environment where failures are unrecoverable and continuous supervision is impossible. This paper presents a Constrained Reinforcement Learning framework for quadrupedal mobile manipulators that learns a single whole-body policy for tracking a 6D end-effector pose specified in task space, with operational limits enforced during learning through a constrained learning mechanism. We introduce a reward formulation in which the transition between locomotion and manipulation emerges from the reward geometry rather than from an explicit gating mechanism, a stability term derived from the Gravito-Inertial Inclination Margin and motivated by the reduced-gravity dynamics of the lunar surface, and a design rule for reward regularization that follows from the multiplicative structure of the termination-based objective. The framework is evaluated in a lunar-analog simulation spanning three terrain morphologies at five difficulty levels under lunar gravity, with regolith contact properties calibrated to the JSC-1a simulant and varied from loose to dense. The learned policy attains mean position and orientation errors of 3.22 cm and 6.83 deg. under nominal conditions, retains this precision across regolith densities and over the operationally representative range of terrain difficulty, and reduces soft-constraint violation time by up to an order of magnitude relative to an unconstrained baseline while incurring no hard-constraint violations.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] AlphaPilot: Multi-Turn Tool-Using LLM Agents for Adaptive Alpha Mining with Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.15488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formulaic alpha mining seeks interpretable expressions that rank assets by future returns. The task is challenging because it demands simultaneous processing of unstructured market descriptions, historical data, and quantitative evaluation of candidate factors, yet most existing methods exploit only a subset of these signals. We introduce AlphaPilot, a reinforcement-learning framework that trains multi-turn tool-using LLM agents for adaptive alpha mining. The agent conditions on market descriptions, proposes factor expressions, queries real-data evaluator feedback, and updates a retained factor pool across turns. This design jointly leverages market text, LLM financial knowledge, real data, and evaluation feedback. At inference time, AlphaPilot performs day-by-day search and pool updates to adapt to shifting market regimes. Across three independent runs in out-of-sample rolling backtests on CSI300 and CSI500, AlphaPilot achieves mean total returns of 42.93% and 54.19%, with mean Sharpe ratios of 2.46 and 2.86, respectively. It attains the highest mean total return, Sharpe, and RankIC among the evaluated methods on both universes.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] SiteEvo: An LLM Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Site-Adaptive Massive MIMO Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.15490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector that is tailored to each specific deployment site can improve detection performance, yet most existing detectors, including deep-unfolding methods, adapt mainly within human-prescribed algorithmic structures. This letter proposes SiteEvo, a site-adaptive agentic discovery framework that extends adaptation from parameter tuning to detector-algorithm discovery. Rather than selecting or recombining predefined architectures, the large language model (LLM) agent synthesizes complete executable detector programs under a common design contract by combining its pretrained communication knowledge, site-specific wireless evidence, and experience accumulated during the search. Each proposal defines its own processing structure and trainable parameterization, and the parameters are optimized by a communication-system backend. The resulting high-performance detector is further structurally refined to reduce block-level computational cost under a bit error rate (BER)-preservation constraint and is finally frozen for deployment without online LLM inference. Simulations across three sites demonstrate BER reductions by factors of 2.6 to 6.0 over the best-performing competing detector at each site at 6 dB, while structural refinement reduces block-level computational cost by 16.7-34.1% under a validation-BER constraint.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Phase-Gated Constrained Reinforcement Learning for End-to-End Capture and Detumbling of Non-Cooperative Targets
item.description: arXiv:2610.15491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active debris removal requires a servicer spacecraft to approach a non-cooperative tumbling object, capture it, and arrest its rotation. This sequence is conventionally divided among phase-specific controllers, each depending on knowledge of the target's inertia, a dedicated grappling fixture, or a hand-designed switch at the contact-rich seam where such pipelines are most fragile. We show that a single constrained reinforcement learning policy can execute the entire mission, driving a dual-arm free-flying servicer from free-space closing through friction-based fixture-free capture to full detumbling of a target whose mass and inertia are unknown and whose state is observed only through noisy estimates. The enabling mechanism is a smooth proximity gate applied at three loci of a constrained Markov decision process. In the reward it induces the phase structure rather than imposing it; in the action space it forecloses a degenerate grab-and-pull exploit as a hard guarantee; and in the constraint set it resolves a normalization failure of constraint-based learning, in which a constraint spanning phases that load it unequally is rendered nearly inert in the phase where precision matters most. Both the failure mode and the remedy apply to any multi-phase problem of this kind. Over 1000 randomized trials the policy succeeds in 99.5% while holding its contact-force, actuator, base-reaction and collision limits throughout, transfers zero-shot to unseen geometries and centre-of-mass offsets, and extrapolates across a tenfold range of target mass.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] When Skills Remain But Access Fails: Factorized Skill Memory for Continual Skill Internalization
item.description: arXiv:2610.15492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skill internalization aims to convert externally specified procedural skills into persistent model capabilities, allowing language-model agents to execute them without retrieving or reinjecting skill descriptions at inference time. Yet when new skills are learned continually, whether previously internalized skills remain usable is still poorly understood. We study forgetting in continual skill internalization and uncover a clear hierarchical structure. Early in subsequent training, a model may lose the ability to invoke an old skill from the raw request, while supplying only the correct canonical skill name substantially restores the learned behavior; with further optimization, this conditional execution also degrades. We call these two stages skill-addressing forgetting and skill-execution forgetting. Guided by this finding, we introduce Factorized Skill Memory (FSM), which separates continual skill memory into a plastic Address Memory and a stable Execution Memory. At each stage, FSM trains a new LoRA executor using only current-stage data, freezes it after acquisition, and appends it to Execution Memory; in parallel, Address Memory incrementally learns to map current requests to executors without replaying historical requests or execution trajectories. At inference time, Address Memory selects one executor from the raw request, and only that frozen executor performs a single language-model generation. On a five-stage benchmark built from 100 TaskBench skills, FSM achieves 65.95% mean exact match and 93.38% addressing accuracy across two task orders, improving over the strongest replay-free parameter-isolation baseline by 14.3 percentage points while remaining within 1.9 points of Replay, which retains historical training examples.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Concept Representations in Vector Space: Quantifying Sharedness and Idiosyncrasy of Meaning
item.description: arXiv:2610.15496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Concepts are the basic units through which we navigate the world and communicate meaning. But do you and I really mean the same thing when we think or speak about a concept? The present study develops a measurement framework for modeling and analyzing interindividual variation in concept representations through sentence embeddings, dense vector representations mapping entire utterances into a shared geometric space. The framework is developed in a theoretical argument and validated, demonstrated, and subjected to robustness checks in a pre-registered study. Short personal definitions, elicited from $N = 125$ participants, are encoded as sentence embeddings and submitted pairwise to a crossed random effects model yielding two concept-level quantities: sharedness ($S_b$), the expected dissimilarity between two randomly drawn individuals, and idiosyncrasy ($I_b$), the person-specific share of total dyadic variance. Two validity tests support the approach: the embedding space fully recovers concept and domain organization from participant definitions even with the target word excluded, and a parameter-free classifier achieves 0.630 accuracy in a within-participant extensional prediction task against a chance baseline of 0.500 and a consistency ceiling of 0.893. The framework finds theoretically interpretable variation in $S_b$ and establishes $I_b$ as a reliable source of dyadic variance across concepts. Results replicate across three encoders varying in architecture and capacity, providing a reproducible and scalable instrument for the empirical study of meaning variation.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Revisited Support Vector Machines: A Unified Joint Optimization Framework with Nystr\"om Approximation for Scalable Adaptive Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.15498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The theoretical elegance of Support Vector Machines (SVMs), grounded in statistical learning theory, establishes them as a reference for robust classification. However, in the era of Big Data, classical SVMs face two major bottlenecks: the prohibitive cubic complexity $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$ of training and the rigidity of static kernels. Traditional methodologies treat kernel selection as a discrete, "brute-force" GridSearch problem, effectively decoupling the learning of data representation from the optimization of the decision boundary. This paper proposes a paradigm shift with a so-called "Revisited SVM", a unified framework that recasts the learning process as a continuous %bi-level joint optimization problem. We derive a novel objective function $J(\alpha, \theta)$ that allows for the simultaneous optimization of dual Lagrange multipliers and kernel hyper-parameters. To solve this challenging non-convex problem efficiently, we introduce a hybrid Block Coordinate Ascent (BCA) algorithm, tightly integrated with Nystr\"om-based low-rank approximation, which drastically reduces computational complexity to $\mathcal{O}(Nm)$. Extensive experiments conducted across four heterogeneous domains (Bioinformatics, Finance, Cybersecurity, and Computer Vision) demonstrate that our approach not only matches but often exceeds exhaustive GridSearch accuracy, while delivering training speedups of up to 100x. Notably, on the complex NSL-KDD intrusion detection dataset, our adaptive kernel approach achieves 96.25\% accuracy compared to a mere 50\% for standard baselines, proving its unique ability to model complex non-linear manifolds in high-dimensional spaces. We validate our results using rigorous statistical tests and provide a theoretical convergence analysis of the proposed algorithm.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Large Decision Models: Repurposing Large Language Models as Single-Pass Decision Makers
item.description: arXiv:2610.15501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models make decisions through parallel prefill and sequential decoding. Although effective, this approach incurs decoding costs and does not explicitly expose decision probabilities. Existing task-specific classifiers require per-task training and offer limited generalization to unseen decision schemas. We propose Large Decision Models (LDMs), repurposing language models to return explicit probabilities over labels specified at run time using one prefill forward pass. We first adapt models to this interface through Diverse Decision Supervision (DDS), covering varied domains, rules and labels. To further narrow the performance gap to a reasoning model, Self-Posed Reasoning Distillation (SPRD) adds tasks generated by a frozen teacher, filters them for answer consistency, and trains on label distributions obtained from repeated teacher reasoning. We evaluate on DecisionVista, pairing new-schema tests with held-out human-labelled sources. Across three base models, the recipe improves accuracy over a step-matched baseline by 1.8 and 1.5 percentage points, respectively, achieving a 182-fold speedup in latency over reasoning rollout on Gemma-4-31B. Reasoning remains stronger on the new-schema test, motivating a confidence router for uncertain decisions. On development sets, routing recovers a median 92% of reasoning's accuracy advantage while generating 27-58% of its tokens. Code is available at https://github.com/JianhuiWei7/LDM.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] From Observations to Authorized Actions: Measuring Source Information in Android Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.15502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Android agents read content from applications and web pages and act on it with the user's authority, yet they cannot reliably tell where that content came from -- its source, the application or document that supplied it. The WebView accessibility fields we inspected expose the host application but omit the document origins available inside the browser, so an agent reading through this interface cannot check which document supplied an object; a limited reproduction on an unmodified WebView yields the same finding. We build and separately evaluate two prototypes to examine how source information supports authorization. Our application-source monitor withholds side-effecting calls whose signed source record contains an untrusted application. With the source set derived from the OS accessibility log, it blocked every selected attack write in the tested runs, but it also withheld benign sends issued after reading untrusted content, flagged benign tasks that use external content, and carried source records into a later clean task. Our WebView source-reference gate uses records from a modified browser to check object origins and reference lifetime through direct calls; in a separate 24-trial evaluation, the live agent selected no disallowed object. Supporting benchmark and planner measurements characterize textual argument matches and attacker-target selection, without establishing causal dataflow or a controlled model ranking. The prototypes are not an integrated defense: the WebView gate still lacks authenticated browser delivery and atomic capture of selected bytes and origin. Together, the results show which source information the tested policies need and why it must stay linked to the object used in execution.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Data Portability Revisited: Toward the Human-Centric, AI-Driven Data Ecosystems of Tomorrow
item.description: arXiv:2610.15503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This Article critically examines the contemporary regulatory framework and discourse surrounding data portability in the United States. Using recent regulatory developments in the European Union as an illustration, this Article suggests that although data access and portability are identified as vital issues in multiple policy instruments, in its current iteration, at least, legal conceptions of portability continue to reinforce the interests of service providers and data controller enterprises rather than individual end users. This Article argues that a paradigm shift toward a more human-centric data approach to data governance must occur, under which data would be recognized as fundamental to an individual's identity in a digital age. Therefore, it should be placed in the hands of individuals rather than service providers or data controller enterprises. This Article considers technical and market trends in the European Union that reveal and facilitate such a change. It suggests that regulatory frameworks should better align with these technological and market developments to encourage change-inducing trends among market actors. In short, this Article identifies a transformative approach to data portability that empowers individuals with the freedom and ability to aggregate their data in secure personal spaces under their control or dominion. Such a human-centric perspective on data portability is crucial in building Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered applications for individual consumers that can pave the way for the human-centric, AI-driven data ecosystems of the future.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Federated Semantic Residuals for Multimodal Recommendation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated Recommendation Systems (FedRSs) learn collaborative scores from interaction histories on device and rank items by them, so a higher score means a higher rank. Item text and images add semantic information that can reorder the list. Existing Federated Multimodal Recommenders (FedMRs) fuse this content into their models, which can obscure how content reorders the list. We therefore propose the SEmantic Residual Adapter (SERA), which keeps content out of an existing FedRS and adds semantic residual scores to its collaborative scores. Content can then lift an item above another only when its semantic residual score exceeds the other's by more than their collaborative score gap. This score grows with the item's content similarity to the user's interaction history and is capped at a residual bound. We prove that for any content, an item can enter the list only if its collaborative score is within twice this bound of the lowest one in the list. A larger bound lets content lift more items, including irrelevant ones, so the bound trades off how far content reaches against accuracy. With a validated bound, SERA improves all three FedRSs on all six datasets without adding personalized parameters. It outperforms FedMRs in most comparisons and lifts some FedRSs above centralized baselines.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Pathwise Alignment for Collaborative Filtering: Bilateral Conditional Flow Regularization
item.description: arXiv:2610.15506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collaborative filtering predicts user-item interactions from implicit feedback. We focus on matrix factorization (MF) trained with the Bayesian Personalized Ranking loss. This loss updates each user embedding only through that user's observed items and sampled negatives, so sparse feedback gives MF few constraints. To constrain each user through other users, we propose Pathwise Alignment for Collaborative Filtering (PACF), which trains MF with one network shared by all training pairs. At points between user and item embeddings, a flow matching term trains the network to predict the user-to-item step, reversed and scaled for sampled negatives. A trajectory consistency term pulls each user's predicted path to end at the observed item. Both terms update the embeddings, so the network is discarded after training, thereby maintaining the efficiency of MF at inference. We prove that a network with bounded sensitivity to its input point accurately fits users who share an item only if their embeddings are close, so these users constrain one another. Against eleven discriminative and generative baselines, PACF achieves the highest performance on all seven datasets. Its relative gains over MF are largest where feedback is sparsest. The shared network thus supplies the missing constraints through other users.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] CacheLink: Functional KV Transport for Zero-Prefill Cross-Model Context Handoff
item.description: arXiv:2610.15509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: KV caches make long-context serving efficient by reusing past computation, but model switching breaks this reuse and forces the receiver to prefill the context again. We study \emph{zero-prefill cross-model context handoff}: translating a sender cache into a receiver-compatible state so that the receiver can continue directly without prefilling same context. Existing affine transport methods show that receiver KV states can be substantially reconstructed from sender caches. However, through extensive analyses, we find that reconstruction fidelity is a poor proxy for receiver utility. Similar K/V reconstruction errors can lead to substantially different attention patterns, predictive distributions, and downstream accuracy, because conventional reconstruction objectives overlook the query-dependent functional importance of K and V in receiver attention. We thus introduce CACHELINK, which learns a coupled K/V correction through the receiver behavior directly. Across four independently trained sender--receiver pairs and seven evaluation panels, CACHELINK improves the equal-weight mean over all methods for every pair. In matched diagnostics, CACHELINK changes K/V squared error by less than 0.4% while substantially changing receiver attention and next-token behavior. At 32K context, it reduces handoff latency by up to $7.27\times$ relative to receiver re-prefill. Our findings verify that reconstruction fidelity alone is insufficient and that preserving the receiver computation induced by the transported cache is important for effective cross-model KV transport.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Structured Stateful Relational Scripts with a High-Quality Dataset for Multi-Shot Audio-Visual Video Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherent multi-shot audio-visual video generation requires maintaining consistent identities while depicting evolving states and coordinating sounds across shot boundaries. Although dense captions describe individual shots in detail, they rarely specify which entities persist, how their states change, or which entities and actions produce sounds. To address this limitation, we propose Structured Stateful Relational Scripts (SSRS), a textual supervision representation that separates persistent entity and voice identities from shot-specific visual and auditory states. SSRS explicitly encodes sound-source bindings and temporal relations, while a global audio-visual event sequence connects local actions and sounds, including events that continue across shot boundaries. We further introduce MSAV-Script-100K, a large-scale dataset of curated multi-shot audio-visual videos paired with detailed SSRS annotations, enabling models to learn identity persistence, state transitions, and event continuity from structured supervision. Experiments demonstrate improvements in cross-shot consistency, adherence to specified state changes, and audio-visual alignment, highlighting the effectiveness of our SSRS and MSAV-Script-100K for coherent multi-shot audio-visual generation. Our proposed dataset is available at \href{https://huggingface.co/datasets/shenlehan/MSAV-Script-100K}{MSAV-Script-100K}.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] REPRO: Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimizer for Automated LLM Red-Teaming
item.description: arXiv:2610.15513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts that bypass their safety training. Existing automated red-teaming methods either require privileged access unavailable in production, rely on manually engineered per-model templates, or optimize a single objective without population-level diversity. We present REPRO (Reflective Evolutionary Prompt Optimization), a pure black-box framework that discovers adversarial prompts through evolutionary optimization driven entirely by a compressed open-weight 7B reflective model on a single consumer GPU. REPRO introduces two mechanisms absent from prior work, both isolated in a component ablation: semantic crossover, an LLM-guided multi-parent recombination operator, and Bayesian strategy selection via Thompson Sampling informed by structured failure analysis. We catalog REPRO's behavior on AdvBench, JailbreakBench, and HarmBench across 36 target models from 11 families, including GPT-5-nano, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-2.5-Pro, and Grok-4.1. Under our protocol REPRO reaches 100\% attack success rate (ASR) on every evaluated target in a single turn, at a median of 24 target queries per behavior. Two properties of the protocol qualify that figure. The judge scoring candidates during optimization also produces the reported ASR, and search halts when it accepts, so ASR reports whether search succeeded within the iteration budget rather than success at a fixed budget. All baseline figures are transcribed from their original papers, which use different judges, budgets, and model versions. We therefore present this as a catalog of model coverage under one protocol rather than a head-to-head ranking, and develop both qualifications in the paper.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] SARATHI: Decoupled Data-Free Probing and Adaptive Reconstruction for Structured LLM Pruning
item.description: arXiv:2610.15514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structured pruning reduces the inference cost of large language models (LLMs) by permanently removing neurons and weight rows, yielding dense, hardware-agnostic speedup. Existing post-training methods couple neuron selection and weight reconstruction through a shared calibration dataset, introducing domain bias and out-of-memory failures at high sparsity. We propose SARATHI, a framework that decouples these two stages. A data-free \emph{NMF Residual Subspace Probe} scores neurons using intrinsic weight geometry, without accessing any calibration data, and carries a formal connection to Robust PCA. \emph{Adaptive OBS} then reconstructs the pruned weights with a localized calibration batch, operating in $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ peak memory per layer and eliminating the global memory bottleneck of coupled methods. A \emph{Bias Shift Compensation} step corrects systematic activation drift in post-LayerNorm architectures that would otherwise cause perplexity collapse at high sparsity. Experiments across six models from two architecture families (gated and non-gated FFN) at 15--40\% sparsity show that SARATHI achieves competitive perplexity and matches or exceeds existing structured pruning baselines on zero-shot accuracy.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Semantically Steerable Image Tokenization
item.description: arXiv:2610.15515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive image tokenizers compress an image into a variable number of tokens matched to its complexity, and recent work makes this allocation controllable: conditioned on a target reconstruction error, the tokenizer itself decides how many tokens an image needs. However, the fidelity measure guiding this allocation shapes which aspects of the image are preserved under compression. The pixel-wise error used in prior work is blind to the spatial structure that carries an image's meaning, and under heavy compression such tokenizers are prone to abruptly discarding tokens that encode essential content. We introduce GIST (Guided Image Semantic Tokenizer), an adaptive tokenizer that can be steered toward a requested semantic fidelity. Its token allocation is jointly controlled by pixel-level and semantic target errors, with semantic error measured in the feature space of a frozen DINOv3 encoder. This joint control enables semantic protection: with the semantic target fixed at zero, the reconstruction target can be relaxed to discard pixel detail while preserving what the image depicts. In a controlled comparison on ImageNet-100, GIST outperforms its pixel-controlled counterpart KARL at every token count, with up to $30\%$ lower LPIPS and $37\%$ lower DreamSim. On average, lowering its semantic target reduces LPIPS $2\times$ faster per token than lowering the reconstruction target, and up to $5\times$ in the low-token regime. Semantic fidelity is thus an effective control signal for adaptive tokenization: it lets a tokenizer see, and so preserve, what an image depicts.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Robust Proportionality Axioms for Additive Utilities
item.description: arXiv:2610.15516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the model of participatory budgeting, in which a subset of candidates is selected subject to a budget constraint. Voters express their preferences by assigning a numerical utility to each candidate. Our focus is on formal analysis of proportionality, a central notion of fairness in multi-winner elections. Intuitively, proportionality means that each group of voters should influence the election outcome roughly in proportion to its size. Recent "plus" axioms of proportionality are particularly appealing notions: they are verifiable in polynomial time, and they provide strong representation guarantees without requiring groups of voters to have cohesive preferences. However, their existing formulations are restricted to approval-based preferences. We generalise extended justified representation plus (EJR+), and Core plus (Core+) to general additive utilities. Our approach builds on a payment-based interpretation of proportionality: candidates' costs are shared among their supporters, with the aim of balancing voters' total payments.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] GNFormer: Gaussian Neural Field Transformer for Efficient Camera-based Occupancy Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2610.15522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Camera-based occupancy prediction provides geometric and semantic scene understanding for robot perception and has been adopted in autonomous vehicle and UAV perception systems. Gaussian primitives offer a promising alternative by potentially representing only occupied regions, thereby concentrating computation and representational capacity where needed and reducing wasted computation and memory in empty space. However, existing Gaussian-based methods suffer from poor primitive utilization, as ineffective training objectives leave some Gaussians in empty space, while the limited expressiveness of Gaussian functions restricts their ability to model complex shapes. To address these limitations, we propose a novel 3D representation, Gaussian Neural Field (GNF), which can accurately map voxel positions to semantic occupancies. In GNF, Gaussians and a neural network jointly parameterize the field, where the Gaussians define its spatial support and provide features for neural decoding, while the neural network enables more expressive occupancy modeling than Gaussian functions alone. We further develop the Gaussian Neural Field Transformer (GNFormer), a streamlined and flexible method that predicts GNFs for camera-based occupancy prediction. Across Occ-ScanNet, SSCBench-KITTI-360, and nuScenes-SurroundOcc benchmarks, GNFormer achieves the highest IoU and mIoU and the fastest inference among the compared single-frame methods. In the experiments, GNFormer can represent indoor and outdoor scenes with only 256 and 1024 Gaussians, respectively, substantially fewer primitives than prior Gaussian-based methods. The code will be released.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Rethinking Evidence Modeling: Context-Coupled Graph Learning for Multimodal Recommendation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal graph recommendation integrates observed interactions with item images and text to learn user preferences. These inputs constitute Semantic-Behavioral Evidence (SBE). Many existing graph methods incorporate collaborative and multimodal semantic relations, yet their aggregation and state updates remain context-separated, limiting the continuous composition of preference evidence across layers and the joint use of multiple sources. To address this limitation, we propose CC-MGRec, a context-coupled graph learning method that organizes SBE within a common graph learning context for cross-relation modeling and compositional propagation. Its context-coupled multimodal graph integrates user-item collaborative relations and item-item semantic relations, coordinating their message scales through joint normalization. Recommendation-grounded semantic calibration uses training behavior to adjust semantic neighbor weights while preserving normalized collaborative propagation coefficients. Collaborative-semantic compositional propagation updates shared node states layer by layer to continuously compose collaborative and multimodal semantic evidence, implicitly forming Preference Evidence Chains (PECs), including collaborative-semantic and visual-textual PECs. Joint execution of relation messages on the same shared node states within each layer preserves propagation outputs while reducing intermediate output processing and fusion overhead. We provide theoretical analysis of the proposed mechanisms. Experiments on three Amazon datasets demonstrate improved recommendation quality and faster inference during graph propagation.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] A Step in the Right Place: Understanding and Optimizing Timestep Placement in Continuous Diffusion Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.15527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous diffusion language models represent an emerging paradigm for language modeling. They generate text in parallel by iteratively refining continuous representations and mapping them back to tokens through a decoder. However, realizing the efficiency advantage of parallel generation requires maintaining generation quality with only a few denoising steps. Even when the number of steps is fixed, their placement along the denoising trajectory remains flexible. In this paper, we demonstrate that changing timestep placement alone can substantially alter the final latent representations and thereby affect the decoded token distributions. Building on these findings, we introduce StepTune, an algorithm that searches for timestep placements that improve generation quality. The search is conducted on a small calibration set and guided by a language-aware objective, with the model and sampling budget fixed. Once calibrated, the timestep placement is fixed and reused across inputs. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in unconditional generation perplexity and conditional task metrics across all evaluated sampling budgets. In particular, StepTune enables 16-step sampling with a frozen model to outperform its native 64-step baseline on both XSum summarization and WMT14 translation and reduces end-to-end latency by approximately $3.8\times$. These results establish timestep placement as a practical means of improving the quality-efficiency trade-off in continuous diffusion language models.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Agent-Canary-Mas: End-to-End Evaluation of Protocol Risk in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.15529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent-to-agent protocols allow LLM agents to discover peers, exchange results, and coordinate tool use. A locally successful protocol attack, however, may be rejected by a later agent or propagated into a consequential task decision. Measuring local exploitability alone leaves this difference unresolved and provides limited evidence about which participant caused the final outcome. We present Agent-Canary-Mas, an end-to-end evaluation system that follows protocol risk through long-horizon multi-agent tasks. It covers five risk classes and 13 subclasses across A2A, ANP, and BCS, with 975 matched malicious--benign task pairs in five business domains. A shared OpenClaw framework runs autonomous, tool-using agents under different underlying models while preserving the task and execution setup. Matched runs separate local protocol success from downstream consequences; retained evidence connects participant selection, message consumption, tool activity, and task-state changes. We further evaluate a protocol-context Guard that checks an object's authority at consequential handoffs. Across three model conditions, local attack success is frequently at or above 90%, while consequence conversion ranges from 7.1\% to 100.0\%. Cross-agent evidence raises macro-averaged Audit-F1 from 29.7% to 95.5%. On Finance tasks, the Guard lowers average ASR from 86.1% to 53.8% and PTCR from 65.5% to 31.2%, with a measurable completion tradeoff. These results show that protocol risk depends on how agents use exchanged objects throughout the task, and that evaluating this path supports more informative risk assessment, attribution, and defense.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Sleep Sound Event Detection Powered by Learnable Multi-Resolution Adaptive Line Enhancer
item.description: arXiv:2610.15532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing, including snoring, hypopnea, and obstructive apnea, is the hallmark of obstructive sleep apnea, whose severity is quantified by the Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI). As conventional polysomnography is costly and clin- ically demanding, microphone-only detection has emerged as a noninvasive alternative for screening. We propose ALE- Confidence Fusion Sound Event Detection (ACF-SED), the first framework that directly injects the per-frame confidence map of an Adaptive Line Enhancer (ALE) into Transformer atten- tion biasing and feature modulation, rather than as mere pre- processing. A Multi-Resolution ALE Bank aggregates three parallel NLMS filters at distinct decorrelation delays, while a Confidence-Guided Cross-Path block couples event and noise streams via gated cross-attention. On the Audio-Polygraphy Dataset for Sleep Apnea Analysis, ACF-SED achieves state- of-the-art detection across Event-F1, Segment-F1, and PSDS, enabling end-to-end AHI estimation.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] UMAS3D: Unified Mask-Free 3D Editing with Region-Adaptive Source Preservation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 3D editing aims to modify an existing 3D asset according to user intent while preserving geometry and appearance outside the intended edit region. Existing methods often rely on task-specific training, source-3D inversion, or external 3D masks, and lack a unified framework for diverse editing conditions and tasks. We propose UMAS3D, a unified 3D editing framework that is training-free, inversion-free, and free from external 3D masks. UMAS3D converts text, bounding boxes, reference images, and their combinations into common target-view guidance, after which addition, deletion, modification, appearance, and pose editing share the same downstream 3D generation process. Our key insight is to couple online edit-region estimation with region-aware source preservation. Mask-Free Adaptive Region Modeling (MARM) initializes an Edit/Keep prior from source-target visual differences and progressively refines it as the target structure evolves, while Source-Guided Preservation Steering (SGPS) constrains the current Keep-region states to retain source geometry and appearance without suppressing target-driven changes. Experiments show that UMAS3D supports addition, deletion, modification, appearance, and pose editing while effectively preserving unedited source content. These advances make UMAS3D a unified framework for flexible and source-preserving 3D editing across diverse editing conditions.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Poisoned into Action: Context Attacks on Typed Decision Workflows
item.description: arXiv:2610.15537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Typed decision interfaces restrict models to predefined actions, yet schema-valid choices can still trigger policy-violating state changes. Evaluating context poisoning thus requires connecting model decisions to execution outcomes while accounting for legitimate automation retained by defenses. We introduce an execution-aware protocol tracing poisoned evidence through retrieval, model choice, automated action, and persisted state. We evaluate it with 1,659 fresh calls to Jev-1.13.0 across 20 development tasks in two synthetic workflows, using three repetitions per condition. Under natural retrieval, a standalone payload reaches all 60 trials and produces five security-violating executions, while a carrier-payload pair exposes the payload in 57 trials and produces one violation. An initial source-exclusion gate blocks the pair's observed violation but also withholds ten otherwise correct attacked decisions and sixteen correct clean decisions. Correcting its empty-scope behavior restores twelve clean decisions without additional model calls. Factorial controls show that adding correct evidence reduces wrong executions from 119/120 to 55/120 in the semantic arm and from 60/120 to zero in the neutral arm, suggesting that much of the improvement reflects general evidence value rather than attack-specific protection. Three prespecified contrasts are not statistically supported after Holm correction, so the findings remain exploratory. The protocol provides an auditable framework for studying which poisoning-induced errors reach execution and how much correct automation defenses preserve. Code is available at https://github.com/WuXixiong/jev-poisoning-bench.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Sensitivity Fidelity Reveals Physical Dependencies Beyond Forecast Accuracy in Deep-Learning Earth-System Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.15540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep-learning models increasingly rival numerical simulation in Earth-system forecasting, yet forecast error alone cannot determine whether their learned input-output dependencies are physically consistent. Here we introduce sensitivity fidelity as an additional criterion: alongside prediction error, model responses to input perturbations should be examined against a trusted reference or established physical knowledge. In an idealized Rayleigh-B\'enard convection benchmark, four surrogate architectures achieved low forecast errors yet encoded markedly different sensitivities. Quantitative comparison with a matched adjoint distinguished the models far more sharply than forecast accuracy and showed that predictive skill and sensitivity fidelity need not coincide, while finite-perturbation experiments further linked these differences to the propagation of initial-condition uncertainty. We then applied this strategy to El Ni\~no-Southern Oscillation prediction, where no adjoint reference exists and learned sensitivities showed event-wise robustness, validity under finite perturbations, and consistency with established precursors. These results identify gradient-based evaluation as a discriminating complement to forecast-error metrics, providing a practical test of whether data-driven Earth-system models learn physically credible dependencies.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Fetch Me If You Can: A Comprehensive Analysis of Fetch Metadata
item.description: arXiv:2610.15541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective server-side defenses against cross-site attacks depend on understanding the context in which browser requests are generated. However, servers often lack the information needed to distinguish legitimate requests from potentially malicious cross-site interactions. Fetch Metadata, a security mechanism introduced in 2019, addresses this limitation by adding a set of HTTP headers to outgoing browser requests. These headers provide servers with information about a request's context and provenance, enabling them to enforce request isolation policies accordingly. However, the extent of Fetch Metadata's real-world adoption and its interaction with existing security mechanisms remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we present the first large-scale measurement study of Fetch Metadata adoption. We analyze the top 1M websites in the Tranco list to detect deployments of Fetch Metadata isolation policies and identify custom policies used in the wild. We then examine how these policies address cross-site threats and assess their security coverage. Finally, we provide the first systematic comparison of Fetch Metadata with existing client-side security mechanisms, revealing security gaps that arise from differences between client-side and server-side enforcement.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Apertus 1.5: From Open Text Models to Open Multimodal Reasoners
item.description: arXiv:2610.15542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models are becoming infrastructure, and infrastructure built in the open, by public institutions, on documented data, is the alternative to dependence on a few providers; Apertus shows this is viable at scale. Apertus 1.5 extends the fully open Apertus family from text to multimodal reasoning. Continued pretraining of the Apertus 1.0 models, on 4T additional tokens for the 8B and 2T for the 70B, adds image and audio understanding and extends the context window fourfold to 262,144 tokens; multimodality enters through the tokenizer, the language-model head remains restricted to text, and the architecture is unchanged. Supervised finetuning, long-context finetuning, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, and preference alignment complete the released models. Thinking is a flag of the chat template rather than a separate model, and lifts mathematical reasoning by up to 20 points on the 8B model. The released models improve over their predecessors on nearly every benchmark; among fully open models of its class, the 8B leads on knowledge, instruction following, and cultural benchmarks, and its instruction following surpasses all compared models, including open-weight ones. On image and audio understanding, a first for the family, the models are competitive with fully open multimodal models, strongest on document understanding and long-form and lower-resource speech recognition, while specialized vision and audio models remain ahead on perception and transcription of English and other high-resource languages. As in Apertus 1.0, we train only on openly available data, respect crawler opt-outs retroactively, and exclude restrictively licensed material. We release the model weights, data preparation and training recipes, and evaluation suites under permissive licenses; openness extends to values, with the Apertus charter guiding alignment stages published alongside the models.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] An Interpretable Linguistically-Grounded Analysis of Scene Saliency in Movie Screenplays
item.description: arXiv:2610.15544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the factors affecting salience in movie screenplay by posing two research questions: 1. {\em Does Uniform Information Density (UID) predict salient scenes?} 2. {\em What other linguistic properties distinguish salient scenes from non-salient background?} We answer both questions through a controlled corpus study on the MENSA corpus, paired with a Linguistically-Grounded Salience Model (LGSM), a dual-stream classifier that fuses a frozen BERT encoder with explicit linguistic features through adaptive gating. The UID picture is layered in long-form discourse. Per-scene UID summaries carry no independent signal once length is controlled, but at the token level salient scenes match non-salient material in the bulk while specifically suppressing the rarest, hardest-to-predict tokens in the upper tail. UID therefore lives at the within-scene token level rather than as a per-scene aggregate. Salient scenes also show a moderate and sustained cast of central characters (following an inverted-U pattern), strong third-person usage, syntactically simpler language, and more abstract vocabulary about motivation and conflict. LGSM exploits this signature and improves recall on salient scenes over a strong semantic baseline while yielding better downstream summaries.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] PointWalker: Mapless Quadruped Locomotion Directly From Raw LiDAR Point Clouds
item.description: arXiv:2610.15548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quadruped robots deployed for inspection and field missions must cross heterogeneous terrain, from stairs, slopes, and gaps to high platforms, stepping stones, and balance beams, where safe support is sparse or see-through. Existing methods interpose a terrain map or a depth image between sensing and control. Maps are costly to maintain, corrupted by odometry drift and outliers, and misled by see-through gratings, while depth cameras degrade with lighting and surface material. In this paper, we present PointWalker, a mapless framework whose single reinforcement learning policy directly consumes raw point clouds from four light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensors. Voxelized points are encoded by linear self-attention and fused with proprioception through cross-attention, so terrain geometry reaches the policy without maps or foothold estimation. One proximal policy optimization (PPO) run, with terrain-aware rewards and dual-channel simulation of see-through gratings, yields one policy for all seven terrain classes with a 90.1% mean success rate in simulation. Deployed zero-shot on a Deep Robotics X30 at 50 Hz onboard, it crosses 0.8-m gaps, climbs 0.8-m platforms and 45{\deg} steel-grating stairs, carries a 50-kg payload, and completes a 2.5-km mountain route.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Rate-Distortion Theory of Gaussian Mixtures via Posterior Label Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.15549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the mean-squared error (MSE) rate-distortion function (RDF) of finite Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in $\mathbb{R}^d$, for which neither the RDF nor an optimal test channel is known in closed form. It can be sandwiched between the genie-aided conditional RDF $R_{\mathbf{X} | T}(D)$, which can be characterized in closed-form for a GMM, and $R_{\mathbf{X} | T}(D)+I(\mathbf{X};T)$, where $T$ denotes the latent component label. We show that the upper bound can be achieved operationally by the proposed Gibbs-relabelling method (GRM), which conveys a label from the posterior $P_{T|\mathbf{X}}$ through \textit{channel simulation} at rate $I(\mathbf{X};T)$, followed by vector quantization of the resulting exactly Gaussian conditional sources by reverse water-filling. Using the Shannon lower bound (SLB), we prove that GRM attains the SLB, and hence the RDF, of a general finite mixture if and only if every component attains its own SLB. For a GMM this holds throughout the fully active interval $D/d<\min_{k,m}\lambda_{k,m}$, where $\lambda_{k,m}$ are the eigenvalues of the component covariances, and for scalar GMMs the condition is also necessary. Since GRM cannot operate below the label cost $I(\mathbf{X};T)$, we propose a complementary stochastic scalar quantization (SSQ) scheme for low rates, which simulates an $M$-ary reconstruction index. We show that at low rates SSQ with $M\geq 2$ matches the Shannon RDF to first order: $R(D_{\max}-\delta)=\delta/(2\tau^2)+o(\delta)$, where $\tau^2$ is a directional sub-Gaussian proxy of the mixture, and quantify the price of a finite codebook through a strict rate gap at high rates and a distortion floor whose joint scaling in $M$ and number of mixture components is characterized. Numerical results illustrate both regimes and the finite-blocklength cost of channel simulation.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] ELECT: Settling Identity Before Rendering for Scalable Story Visualization
item.description: arXiv:2610.15555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training-free story visualization without reference images must preserve recurring entities across frames while scaling to long narratives. Existing methods typically maintain consistency by conditioning each frame on other frames of the same story, coupling generation time, VRAM, or both to story length. We introduce ELECT, which instead settles cross-frame identity before final rendering through a language-guided scene-entity mapping and stationary anchors elected from the model's own drafts. This makes the per-frame cost of the final rendering pass independent of story length. Joint attention exceeds 96 GB of VRAM at 32 scenes, whereas ELECT remains at 8.3 s per frame and under 20 GB VRAM from 10 to 1000 scenes. On the Story50 long-story benchmark, ELECT reaches 0.833 average Character Consistency Similarity (aCCS), compared with 0.826 for ten-round refinement, at one seventh of its generation cost, with lower text alignment (0.327 vs. 0.340). At 1000 scenes, to our knowledge, the first evaluation of training-free story visualization at this length, ELECT exceeds ten-round refinement by 0.017 aCCS and the nearest flat-cost baseline by 0.091, while also surpassing refinement in text alignment at one twenty-fourth of its generation time. These results show that long-horizon consistency need not require increasingly expensive inter-frame conditioning as stories grow.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Vision-Predictor-Action: Towards Efficient Embodied AI via Neuro-Symbolic JEPA Predictors
item.description: arXiv:2610.15556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models commonly generate robot actions token by token through Large Language Model (LLM) decoders, causing inference latency to grow with action sequence length and limiting closed-loop control frequency. We present Goal-Conditioned Vision-Predictor-Action (VPA), which replaces autoregressive decoders with a lightweight latent control loop. A shared vision encoder and a frozen text encoder embed observations, goal images, and instructions; a neuro-symbolic selector chooses a discrete skill; a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) predictor forecasts the next latent state; and a flow-matching solver generates an entire action chunk in a few integration steps, so that sequential network evaluations per decision step do not depend on the action horizon. We analyze inference complexity, regularization against representation collapse, and conditions under which latent sub-goal thresholding limits error accumulation across task phases. As an initial proof of concept, we evaluated VPA on the LIBERO-10 suite. The trainable model has under 20M parameters (checkpoint under 75 MB, excluding a frozen 63.4M-parameter CLIP text encoder); a decision step of a single-camera reference configuration takes 10-14 ms on an Apple M4; and trained only on LIBERO-10 demonstrations in under three hours on a single GPU, a two-camera policy succeeded in 40.0% of 200 evaluation episodes. These preliminary results from a single training run suggest the approach is workable. Code and weights are available at https://github.com/ylee-sling/Vision-Predictor-Action and https://huggingface.co/ylee-sling/vpa-libero10, and archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22960920.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Stereo-Planner: Learning Stereo-to-Trajectory Planning for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Quadrotor Navigation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing navigation systems commonly rely on dedicated depth sensors or explicit depth reconstruction, while learning to generate trajectories directly from RGB images remains challenging due to the sim-to-real domain gap. In this work, we propose Stereo-Planner, an end-to-end vision-to-trajectory framework that enables zero-shot sim-to-real planning from stereo RGB observations. The key idea is to formulate trajectory generation as state- and scale-conditioned querying of latent stereo geometry. A Scene Representor incorporates a pretrained vision grounding foundation model to extract geometric cues shared across simulated and real-world environments, supporting generalization across visual domains. A lightweight Trajectory Decoder then translates these representations into trajectories through interleaved attention, separating trajectory-state interaction from scene-feature retrieval and incorporating the stereo baseline as a metric-scale cue. With these designs, Stereo-Planner is trained entirely on simulated data by minimizing differentiable trajectory costs and deployed directly in real-world environments without fine-tuning. Benchmark results demonstrate strong cross-scene generalization, with a 95% success rate in simulation environments at a commanded speed of 8 m/s, and competitive performance against depth-based planners using only stereo RGB observations for scene perception. Furthermore, deployment on a compact quadrotor equipped with an NVIDIA Orin NX enables autonomous flight at speeds of up to 7 m/s, with a mean onboard vision-to-action inference time of 24.27 ms. The software, simulation environments, and hardware designs will be open-sourced at https://github.com/Stereo-Planner/Stereo-Planner.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] A Plausible Future Is Not a Causal Future: Can Video Models Generate How the World Unfolds?
item.description: arXiv:2610.15562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale video generation models are increasingly viewed as a promising path toward world models, yet their ability to capture causally coherent physical dynamics remains poorly understood. Existing evaluations largely emphasize visual quality, prompt adherence, or broad physical plausibility, leaving open whether a model can faithfully realize a complete causal cascade, in which an initiating event propagates through causally dependent interactions to a terminal outcome. We introduce CausalCascade, a simulator-grounded benchmark centered on 50 event-rich Blender scenes with structured event graphs, graph-grounded diagnostic VQA, three levels of future-event specification, and 2,832 controlled counterfactual variants, and use it to evaluate nine image-to-video models with complementary motion-, event-, and counterfactual-level diagnostics. Across the evaluated models, generated motion is more reliably localized spatially than realized with correct spatiotemporal evolution, while richer future-event specification improves event recovery but leaves physical realization limited. Counterfactual evaluation further reveals weak selective responsiveness to physical interventions, while most audited failures are foundational, arising at scene consistency or event occurrence. Together, these results position causal cascade generation as a process-level test of world modeling and highlight the need to jointly recover the intended future, faithfully realize its physical evolution, selectively respond to physical interventions, and maintain a coherent physical world over time. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/SJTU-DeepDeltaLab/CausalCascade .
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Anticipatory Textile MMG-Strain Sensing for Confirm-Then-Assist Soft Knee Exosuits
item.description: arXiv:2610.15563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Soft wearable robots must commit to assistance around movement onset, when the available signals are ambiguous. Surface electromyography (sEMG) detects neuromuscular drive early but degrades under sweat and electrode shift, and kinematic sensors respond only once the limb moves. This letter presents a knitted textile interface that co-samples a three-channel mechanomyography (MMG) array and an anterior strain sensor on a single synchronous 500 Hz clock. Across five participants, MMG activation preceded strain-detected knee motion during sit-to-stand by per-channel medians of 322-344 ms. Sampled on the same clock, the sign of the strain slope resolved movement direction on 649 of 650 completed transitions with no training or per-participant calibration, raising four-class balanced accuracy from 90.3% to 95.6%. The fused signals drove a two-stage confirm-then-assist policy for a soft pneumatic knee. Across 240 trials in four participants, the onboard controller entered the assist state on 78 of 80 sit-to-stand trials and on none of the 80 isometric co-contractions. It also entered the assist state on 27 of 80 stand-to-sit trials and left it at the hold timeout, motivating an antagonistic flexor gauge to resolve this direction at onset. Co-sampling muscle acoustics with textile strain on one clock lets the inflation command be issued around movement onset.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] UNISON: A Unified Framework for Learning from Scored Bags
item.description: arXiv:2610.15564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce UNISON, a unified framework that bridges multiple instance learning and recommendation systems by treating both as instances of learning from scored bag collections of (item, score) pairs. Unlike traditional approaches that address bag-level classification and personalized recommendation as separate problems, UNISON decomposes learning into three interconnected stages: (1) learning universal item representations, (2) modeling bag-specific preference patterns through lightweight personalized parameters, and (3) inferring bag-level characteristics from learned preferences. We justify the architectural choice of linear bag-specific scoring through a first-order analysis: when item embeddings are sufficiently smooth in the score, a linear function approximates the score up to a Taylor remainder controlled by the curvature of the underlying preference function. For cold-start scenarios, we show that the cold-bag fitting problem reduces to ridge-less linear regression with a closed-form solution, and provide convergence guarantees for the iterative variant. Empirically, UNISON matches or outperforms state-of-the-art approaches across diverse domains: entertainment (books, movies), immunology (T cell receptor (TCR) based classification), and microbiome, offering superior computational efficiency and interpretability. A controlled synthetic experiment further confirms that the bag-specific parameters ($w_j, b_j$) recover the latent factors that drive item scores even when the projection $\phi$ has no access to the original scoring mechanism (AUC > 0.998). UNISON is available at https://github.com/louzounlab/UNISON.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Genesis: Visual Augmentation Primitives for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
item.description: arXiv:2610.15565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent multimodal large language models achieve promising results on visual reasoning tasks, approaching human-level performance on existing STEM benchmarks. However, these capabilities degrade under complex real-world scenes. We identify that chain-of-thought reasoning remains largely confined to the linguistic space, rarely anchoring each step in visual evidence. The main cause is the absence of such data during training. In this work, we introduce a training data augmentation pipeline, \textbf{Visual Augmentation Primitives} (VAP), which leverages state-of-the-art vision generative models to synthesize diverse photorealistic training samples and corresponding reasoning text. VAP introduces some basic operators and applies them to a seed image and gets a variant. It also constructs coherent multimodal reasoning chains throughout the generation process. Such training data force models to perceive visual content and perform logical reasoning according to them at every step. We further introduce multimodal chain-of-thought rubric-based reinforcement learning to enhance this. It rewards not only text reasoning but also visual reasoning by scoring intermediate reasoning steps for logical validity, completeness, and consistency. Moreover, we construct the UNREAL benchmark to systematically evaluate visual reasoning on hyperrealistic scenes across controllable difficulty levels. Experiments show that a 4B model built on this framework surpasses 8B baselines, with performance improving consistently as the model scales to 32B, validating the scaling law for visual reasoning.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] The Evolution of In-Premise Networks In the Era of Immersive Services: From Copper to Fiber-to-The Room [Invited Tutorial]
item.description: arXiv:2610.15566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The telecommunications industry is shifting toward an experience-driven era defined by immersive applications that impose stringent network demands. While passive optical network (PON)-based Fiber-To-The-Home (FTTH) architectures have historically delivered high-capacity broadband, a growing performance gap between access and indoor networks necessitates driving fiber deeper into premises. Complementing existing copper and WiFi technologies, Fiber-to-the-Room (FTTR) is emerging as a critical enabler. This article examines the drivers of this architectural shift, specifically focusing on collaborative extended reality (XR). We analyze the multi-modal traffic characteristics and Quality-of-Experience (QoE) requirements of XR, alongside the resulting network performance implications. To address these demands, we propose a novel resource allocation framework integrating coarse-grained traffic forecasting with intelligent in-premise roaming. This framework facilitates the flexible deployment of artificial intelligence models tailored to the computational capabilities of the FTTH, FTTR, and WiFi segments. Numerical evaluations of a representative multi-tier network demonstrate that long-horizon, multi-step-ahead traffic forecasts significantly reduce inference frequency. This approach enables coordinated resource allocation and network-orchestrated seamless mobility across rooms, effectively satisfying collaborative XR QoE requirements. Finally, we highlight strategies to amortize FTTR capital expenditure by extending the optical infrastructure's role beyond basic connectivity. By supporting diverse services over a unified physical layer, FTTR enhances infrastructure utilization, unlocks novel revenue streams, and maximizes the value of in-premise fiber deployments.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Reviewing Beyond the Change: Repository Size and Existing Code Across Agent and Human Pull Requests
item.description: arXiv:2610.15567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reviewers sometimes name existing repository items outside the change under review. We ask whether such references are more common in larger repositories, and whether the pattern differs between agent-authored and human-authored pull requests. An instrument resolves names in inline review comments against the base-commit repository; size-matched negative controls estimate chance matches.
