Among 92,042 comments on agent pull requests in 2,034 GitHub repositories, 6.5 per cent name an existing item outside the change. An internally pre-specified log-linear model finds an odds ratio of 1.35 per tenfold increase in code files (interval 1.15 to 1.59), and size-matched negative controls indicate that chance matching does not account for the rise. Exploratory analyses suggest that the association is concentrated from small to mid-sized repositories and is imprecise among large ones. Human pull requests in 1,845 of these repositories show a similar association. A pre-specified comparison finds a small agent excess just within the bound set as negligible, but the evidence does not establish a robust agent-specific difference. The instrument misses many references, so reported shares likely understate prevalence, and the validation cannot estimate how recall changes with repository size.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Truncation Samplers Are Nested: Comparing Decoding Rules Is a Measurement Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.15570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Settling one comparison between two truncation samplers has cost six thousand A100-hours, and nothing says in advance how far apart two samplers can be. We observe that almost every deployed truncation rule keeps a prefix of the probability-sorted vocabulary, so any two such rules are nested at every decoding step. Nesting yields a closed-form per-step distance and a coupling under which both samplers emit identical text until they first disagree. Accumulated over a generation, this gives a separation certificate that bounds the difference between two samplers on any bounded outcome, is computable from logs a comparison already produces, and equals their sequence-level total variation distance exactly when neither rule ever overtakes the other. Two consequences follow without measurement: exactness is fragile, and certifying a small difference requires the two retained masses to agree to very high precision at every step. On six open-weight models over four math and science benchmarks, the certificate for every hyperparameter grid we tested is at least 0.998, so a bound alone rarely settles a comparison, although two members of one family can be far closer. What remains useful is the coupling, which gives an unbiased paired estimator that cuts variance $1.2$-$3.8\times$ against prompt-level pairing. Read against benchmark sizes at the default pair's variance and our point estimate of its between-prompt component, resolving a one-point difference needs 8 to 32 samples per prompt on GSM8K, MATH-500 and GPQA-Diamond and about 210 on AIME 2025; at that component's upper confidence bound GPQA-Diamond needs more than 32 and AIME 2025 cannot be resolved at any sample count. Choosing a truncation sampler is a measurement problem at least as much as a design one. The code is available at https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/truncation-samplers.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Look Before You Move: Agent-Interface-Aligned Supervision for Open-World Mobile Manipulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-world mobile manipulation requires a robot to find an object, approach it, and move it to a target receptacle from a language instruction. Training vision-language model (VLM) agents for these tasks requires demonstrations of both action selection and active vision. Existing pipelines often convert planned trajectories into high-level action labels, but shortest-path progress provides limited supervision for deciding where to look. We introduce Agent-Interface Data Alignment (AIDA), a data collection pipeline in which a teacher directly selects and executes actions through the deployed agent's skill interface. For mobile manipulation, we design teachers that maintain target visibility, recover lost targets, and approach for picking or placing. We add template-based spatial reasoning supervision and use a shared harness to organize observations, history, and outputs during training and inference. The resulting agent, AIDA-OWMM, achieves 71.76% full-task success on 170 held-out OWMM episodes. Teacher sensitivity analysis shows that active-vision demonstrations improve student success. The simulation-trained agent achieves 38% end-to-end success on a real mobile robot without additional training. Applying AIDA to a navigation subset of EmbodiedBench further demonstrates the pipeline's utility for navigation tasks.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Walk-on-Ambient-Patch: Solver-Adapted Isometric Embeddings for Projected Walk on Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.15573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Projected Walk on Spheres (PWoS) solves surface PDEs through ambient sampling and closest-point projection, but tightly folded embeddings can force short steps or ambiguous projections despite simple intrinsic geometry. We introduce Walk-on-Ambient-Patch (WoAP), which treats the embedding as a solver variable. Edge-isometry constraints and tangent-point repulsion separate intrinsically distant regions, optionally in higher codimension; patch states track residual projection branches without introducing PDE boundaries. We analyze the resulting geometry--sampling tradeoff: additional dimensions provide separation freedom but reduce uniform tangent progress, while strong tangent-biased proposals incur large importance-weight moments. Folded-surface experiments demonstrate reduced projection conflicts, a separate hard-constraint pilot verifies metric preservation, and an internal fixed-RMSE comparison favors higher dimensions at stricter accuracy targets. Together, these results motivate choosing the embedding and projection state jointly with the stochastic solver.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] The Fragility and Dynamics of LLM Pruning-Recovery Steps
item.description: arXiv:2610.15574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structural pruning followed by a recovery stage is the standard recipe for compressing large language models (LLMs), yet the two stages are typically designed and tuned in isolation. In this work, we study how their interaction shapes the compressed model, sweeping ordering, the data that drives each stage, and the alignment of their training objectives. We find that instruction-following is the first capability to collapse under pruning, well before knowledge, reasoning, or core language modeling, and that much of the pruning in-domain loss is likely not knowledge loss but a domain-agnostic failure to respond coherently to the prompt. We find in our setting that in-domain data is the strongest pruning signal, whereas instruction-style data recovers the most. Stage order matters little, but only marginally. We further analyze how the importance ranking drifts before and after pruning. Together these results give practitioners a concrete recipe for composing pruning and recovery.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Self-Representation Alignment in Diffusion Models for Video Background Music Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion models have been widely used for various generative tasks. However, recent studies have demonstrated that the internal representations learned in the diffusion models' denoising process are insufficiently meaningful, which can hinder the generation performance. To address this, we propose a novel diffusion U-Net architecture enhanced by explicitly aligning the weaker representation from the earlier layer conditioned on higher noise with the better representation from the later layer conditioned on lower noise during training, which we use for the challenging multimodal task of video background music generation. Our diffusion U-Net Self-Representation Alignment (U-SRA) employs an alignment loss to effectively guide our diffusion model to learn good internal representations, thereby enabling it to produce higher-quality symbolic music conditioned on video features. We employ a cross-attention mechanism to synchronize music with video segments. Experiments on a benchmark video-music dataset demonstrate that the proposed U-SRA approach for video background music generation surpasses the state-of-the-art across key evaluation metrics, including video-music alignment and overall music quality.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] SIGN-MAPPO: State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X
item.description: arXiv:2610.15577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooperative driving at mixed-traffic unsignalized intersections is challenged by imperfect vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication, human-driven vehicle (HV) intentions that cannot be directly communicated, and the potential incompatibility of independently generated crossing decisions. This paper proposes State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X (SIGN-MAPPO) to address these challenges through three coordinated mechanisms. Each decision-eligible connected and automated vehicle (CAV) first reconstructs a receiver-specific traffic graph from its ego state and the peer-state records available to it, from which a shared graph-attention policy generates a raw Stop/Go intention augmented with predicted HV-intent features. CAV intentions are then exchanged through timestamped vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) messages, and a local conflict-aware arbitration layer converts each CAV's intention into a safe executable action despite potentially inconsistent peer information. In the principal Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) evaluation, SIGN-MAPPO achieves a 97.53% completion rate, a 0.10% collision rate, and a mean intersection traversal time of 35.28 s. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary contributions of HV-intent prediction and CAV-intent exchange to this performance. The trained policy also remains robust under the evaluated communication-delay and packet-loss ranges, and cross-scenario tests show complete traffic clearance across the tested settings, though safety margins narrow under compound unpredictable HV behavior.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Towards Robust Calibration Dataset for Domain-General Mixture of Experts Pruning
item.description: arXiv:2610.15578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training expert pruning is a promising deployment technique for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. The calibration set is an integral part of the pruning process, however, its correlation with evaluation performance is largely misunderstood and unintuitive. In this work, we present an empirical study of the robustness of calibration perturbations, specifically in MoE models. Showing how calibration size, language, and data distribution affect layer-wise expert pruning for gpt-oss-20b. Our findings reveal that (1) domain-general pruning quality receives minimal benefit from scaling calibration data beyond small sample sizes, (2) cross-lingual calibration transfers effectively, with English-only calibration maintaining strong performance across seven languages of varying typologies and scripts, and (3) a diverse calibration data resembling the pretraining distribution can yield comparable or superior performance to test-distribution data. Ultimately, we provide practical insights as a recipe for better understanding calibration for more effective domain-general expert pruning.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Approximation Algorithms for Dual-Memory Request Scheduling in Disaggregated LLM Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.15579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disaggregated LLM inference executes the prefill and decode phases on separate resource pools, reducing interference between the two phases. However, this architecture introduces a coupled scheduling problem because a request that completes prefill retains its prompt KV cache in prefill memory until it is admitted to the decode pool. Prefill and decode admission decisions therefore jointly determine memory occupancy and request completion times. To the best of our knowledge, this problem lacks a formal formulation, and no approximation guarantees are known for request scheduling in disaggregated LLM inference. We formalize this setting as the dual-memory request scheduling (DMRS) problem, whose objective is to minimize the sum of request completion times, and prove that it is strongly NP-hard. We develop two deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithms. The first applies to instances satisfying $\alpha<1$ and $\beta<1$ and achieves an approximation ratio of $8+\frac{4}{1-\alpha}+\frac{8}{1-\beta}$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the maximum normalized prefill and peak decode memory demands among all requests, respectively. In particular, it yields a $32$-approximation when $\alpha,\beta\leq 1/2$. The second algorithm applies to all feasible instances and achieves a uniform $36$-approximation. Finally, evaluations on two H100 GPUs using trace-derived offline workloads show that the proposed algorithms reduce the sum of request completion times relative to multiple vLLM deployment baselines.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Ellipsoids from Tangents
item.description: arXiv:2610.15580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for detecting and fitting multiple ellipsoids in 2D, 3D and higher-dimensional data. The representation is based on tangents to the ellipsoid together with their contact points, rather than on points alone. A tangent contributes d independent equations where a point contributes one, so each hypothesis needs fewer samples, which in turn reduces the number of iterations required to recover every ellipsoid. The problem is posed as sets of linear equations whose solutions -- the ellipsoid parameters -- are recovered robustly by clustering in parameter space. The algorithm works in all dimensions and outperforms the state of the art in 2D. The approach applies in general to the robust solution of linear equations, and so has utility beyond ellipsoid fitting.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Coarse-Grained Predictive Resource Allocation Framework enabling In-Premise XR Collaborations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Immersive extended reality (XR) applications are key enablers of human-centric connectivity in next-generation networks. However, meeting their high-throughput, ultra-low-latency, and high-reliability demands while preventing cyber-sickness remains a critical challenge, especially in environments with non-deterministic wireless connectivity. Fiber-To-The-Room (FTTR), extending widely deployed Fiber-To-The-Home (FTTH) infrastructure, offers a promising solution. Yet, satisfying the stringent Quality-of-Experience (QoE) requirements of XR collaborators demands robust resource allocation across the multi-tier cascade of FTTH, FTTR, and WiFi segments. In this paper, we propose a coarse-grained traffic forecasting-empowered proactive resource allocation and intelligent in-premise roaming framework. Here, artificial intelligence (AI) model complexities are scaled to the computational capabilities of each network segment. At the FTTR segment, we employ a hybrid temporal convolutional and bi-directional long short-term memory (TCN-BiLSTM) network for multi-modal XR traffic forecasting, integrating passive optical network (PON) and WiFi access points with multi-link operation (MLO) and orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA). The resulting long-horizon forecasts reduce inference frequency, enabling coordinated FTTR-WiFi resource allocation and seamless network-orchestrated mobility across rooms. At the FTTH segment, we deploy Transformer-based time-series models (e.g., Informer, Autoformer, PatchTST, and TFT) to predict the complex XR traffic aggregated in FTTR segments for transmission over the FTTH backhaul. Evaluations show Transformer-based models are up to $\sim$75% more accurate in long-horizon forecasting than the hybrid model. Extensive simulations confirm the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional methods in satisfying XR QoE requirements.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Inverse Garment Design with Visual Agents
item.description: arXiv:2610.15582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of inverse garment design, reconstructing simulation-ready 3D outfits with arbitrary layers from a single image, with visual agents. Unlike differentiable optimization that is time-consuming, or feed-forward methods limited by training data, we introduce DressAgent, a hierarchical agentic system that recovers garment sewing patterns through planning and closed-loop refinement grounded in physical simulation. To this end, we first present an enhanced representation based on GarmentCode for diverse styles and arbitrary dressing layers, and build the first multi-layer sewing pattern dataset with over 15K outfits for supervision and benchmarking. Inverse design then proceeds coarse to fine: In layer planning and coarse estimation, agents infer layer order and relations, peel each layer into its own view, and estimate coarse patterns. In fine-grained refinement, an agentic trio of Tailor, Critic, and Orchestrator refines patterns in a closed loop of editing, simulating, and judging against the reference with visual and measured evidence. Carefully designed tools and an evolving memory make this refinement converge on the target geometry. We also design an agentic generation method for high-fidelity textures. DressAgent outperforms feed-forward methods by a large margin, surpasses or matches differentiable optimization in a fraction of the time, and generalizes to complex layering, diverse poses, and body shapes.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] StreamingWAM: Streaming World Action Modeling via Chunk-Wise Staircase Flow Matching
item.description: arXiv:2610.15585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World Action Models (WAMs), often built upon pretrained video-generation world models, have emerged as a promising framework for general-purpose and open-ended robot control. However, their real-world deployment often suffers from discontinuous and jerky execution. Existing methods typically address this issue by either improving inference efficiency or enhancing action continuity across prediction chunks, without jointly addressing both challenges. To bridge this gap, we propose StreamingWAM, a streaming-diffusion framework for WAM-based robot control. StreamingWAM combines a noise ladder for chunk-wise action prediction, a prefix rollout module for cross-chunk continuity, and dense video-history memory for temporally consistent conditioning. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world robotic tasks demonstrate that StreamingWAM improves action continuity across static and dynamic settings, achieving competitive performance while reducing steady-state replanning latency to 72.9 ms in simulation and 57.3 ms on the real robot. The method also produces smoother action transitions, while the streaming staircase reduces sensitivity to the execution horizon K.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] An Attention-Guided Graph Neural Network Surrogate for Boundary Integral Computation in Physical Field Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2610.15590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In practical engineering and scientific computing, a real physical system can be reduced to a boundary value problem, and the adequate boundary information to determine the interior spatial distribution and evolutionary state of the physical field can be solved with linear equations, alternatively, the the real physical problem can be treated with boundary problems with in adequate information problems in field of machine learning. This paper proposes a deep learning framework for the recovery of missing boundary information using an attention-guided graph neural network (GNN) surrogate. The framework extracts features from the physical information on the discretized boundary into a latent space, and the missing boundary quantities are then predicted by the network. Thus, the nonlinear mapping from known boundary quantities to missing boundary quantities is learned using a variational autoencoder (VAE) architecture, while an attention mechanism is incorporated to better model the correlations among different types of boundary information. Furthermore, the interior physical field can be reconstructed using the conventional boundary element method (BEM) integral formulation. The effectiveness of the GNN-BEM framework is evaluated using numerical examples of the two-dimensional Laplace and Poisson equations, which demonstrate good performance in reconstruction accuracy, local detail preservation, and model stability. The results show that GNN-BEM provides a feasible computational framework for boundary information recovery and fast interior physical field reconstruction for partial differential equations under complex boundary conditions.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] FireNav: Decision-Oriented Reconstruction Evidence Routing for Vision-Language Navigation in Indoor Fire Environments
item.description: arXiv:2610.15595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In real-world indoor fire environments, visual degradation severely impairs instruction grounding, waypoint prediction, and long-horizon exploration in vision-language navigation (VLN). Although image restoration offers a natural means to mitigate such visual degradation, existing methods primarily optimize reconstruction fidelity, which does not necessarily translate into better navigation decisions and may even corrupt task-critical cues when applied indiscriminately. In this paper, we present FireNav, a decision-oriented reconstruction evidence routing framework that aligns visual restoration with navigation utility in VLN. To advance this task, we first contribute FireVLN-Bench, a paired indoor fire navigation benchmark with clean references preserving task semantics, safety supervision, and matched settings for continuous navigation and robot execution with simulated dynamics. Our FireNav retains native visual tokens and treats latent reconstruction features as auxiliary evidence, where a lightweight router leverages visual features, task context, and prior execution states to determine whether such evidence should be admitted and how strongly it should contribute to the visual tokens. To learn when reconstruction is beneficial, we further introduce decision utility calibration, which compares action prediction losses with and without candidate evidence under the same state, thereby supervising evidence selection according to its contribution to waypoint, heading, and arrival prediction. Experiments demonstrate that FireNav consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both navigation success and path efficiency across evaluation settings.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Almost Lossless Transfer for Cuttable Distributed Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.15596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study constant-round LOCAL approximation for additive local vertex-subset minimization problems. Given a $k$-uniform $\alpha$-approximation on a hereditary source class closed under disjoint union, Bonamy, Das, Gavoille, Picavet, Suomela, and Wesolek obtained ratio $\alpha(d+1)+1$ on locally nice target classes of asymptotic dimension $d$. We prove two transfers with ratios $\alpha+1+\eta$ and $\alpha+\eta$ for every $\eta>0$. These bounds require the stronger local niceness assumption at a larger scale that depends on $\eta$. The first algorithm keeps their repair construction and increases the radius used to detect errors. We average over partitions of the graph to bound the retained cost without the factor $d+1$. These partitions are used only in the analysis. The second algorithm tests several deletion widths around the errors. In each component of the repair zone, it chooses a smallest union of retained choices and an exact repair. Averaging over the widths bounds the cost counted twice and yields ratio $\alpha+\eta$. Both transfers are deterministic and computable, use arbitrary distinct numerical identifiers, and need no knowledge of the graph size. Their outputs also satisfy local uniformity guarantees. For 2-domination on graphs of bounded Euler genus, the same planar source gives ratio $19$ through the earlier transfer and $6+\eta$ through ours. For minimum dominating set, our transfer gives ratio $7+\varepsilon$ on graphs formed by attaching a clique of arbitrary size at one vertex of a planar graph, using the source algorithm of Amiri and Siebertz. This class satisfies our target assumptions and allows nonempty error sets. Its Euler genus is unbounded, so their guarantee for graphs of bounded Euler genus does not cover the whole class.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Side-Vent Design for Microphone-Based Mechanomyography Sensors: Modeling and Experimental Evaluation of Contact Dependence
item.description: arXiv:2610.15600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wearable muscle sensing for rehabilitation, assistive robotics, and electrical-stimulation feedback needs mechanomyography sensors less sensitive to fit changes during wear. In microphone-based mechanomyography, cavity pressure depends on rim contact, a dependence housing design has rarely targeted. This study evaluates a side-vented housing, whose vent opens a pressure-relief path in parallel with the rim to lower contact dependence, and quantifies the acoustic-gain cost. Thermoviscous finite-element simulations compared twenty cavity configurations under prescribed source motion. Paired bench sweeps over 10-200 Hz on both housings compared direct contact with a Gap-ring spacer, a radially grooved spacer ring. At 100 Hz, side venting reduced the simulated acoustic-gain variation across 0.10-0.50 mm rim clearances from 25.8 to 10.0 dB and cost 5.5 dB of gain at 0.20 mm clearance. Velocity fields and branch-flow calculations identified this path. At the higher speaker drive level, the Gap-ring spacer caused median attenuations of 13.6 dB (vented) and 30.1 dB (unvented) relative to direct contact. In this front end, a 35.9-dB signal-gain increase at 100 Hz raised the calculated operational-amplifier voltage-noise gain by 1.6 dB. A single-participant demonstration of paced elbow flexion and extension compared envelope timing and spectra between housings, finding similar envelope timing (correlation 0.935) and broadly similar spectra (correlation 0.956). Vent area trades acoustic gain against contact dependence and can therefore serve as a housing design parameter.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] CondMSP: Condition-Informed and Resource-Aware Inorganic Materials Synthesis Planning
item.description: arXiv:2610.15603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Materials synthesis planning (MSP) connects AI-driven materials discovery to experimental realization by proposing precursors, synthesis operations, and processing conditions for a target material. Existing approaches predict these components separately or in pairs and treat conditions only as a prediction target. Consequently, MSP remains centered on recipe prediction: it leaves unexplored how conditions can serve as process context for constructing synthesis routes, and it does not address which candidate routes should be executed under limited experimental resources. We propose CondMSP, which extends MSP from recipe prediction to execution-aware planning. CondMSP predicts temperature, time, and atmosphere by combining a joint predictor with variable-specific experts, and then uses these predictions both as process context, grounding the generation and retrieval of operation sequences, and as execution requirements, specifying which thermal stages can share a furnace run and at what cost. This specification is held fixed across all compared methods; within it, CondMSP ranks routes across precursor sets by a common utility and, under furnace budgets, jointly selects routes and allocates their thermal stages by constrained optimization. CondMSP improves condition and operation prediction and, under this shared constraint, raises reference-recipe recovery from 27.9% to 32.9% at three simulated furnace runs per target and from 34.7% to 40.0% at 30 trials, while a new evaluation set of 2,344 targets supports generalization beyond oxide-dominated training chemistry.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Squeeze-Aware-YOLO: Early Channel Recalibration and Multi-Scale Fusion for Real-Time Traffic Sign Detection
item.description: arXiv:2610.15604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traffic sign detection plays a vital role in intelligent transportation systems, supporting the safe operation of advanced driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles. Despite significant progress in real-time object detection, accurately identifying traffic signs under challenging conditions remains difficult. Variations in lighting, adverse weather, motion blur, and partial occlusion often reduce detection performance, especially for small or visually degraded signs where important spatial information can be lost. To address these challenges, we propose Squeeze-Aware-YOLO, a lightweight traffic sign detection framework that introduces a multi-branch bottleneck module combining convolutional kernels of different sizes with a Squeeze-and-Excitation mechanism to improve feature extraction and adaptive channel weighting. In addition, we integrate the Multi-Branch Auxiliary Feature Pyramid Network and Re-parameterized Heterogeneous Multi-Scale modules to strengthen multi-scale feature representation and feature fusion while preserving real-time inference efficiency for practical deployment. The proposed approach is evaluated on the Bangladeshi Traffic Sign Detection Dataset, the CSUST Chinese Traffic Sign Detection Benchmark 2021, and the German Traffic Sign Detection Benchmark, achieving mAP@0.5 scores of 74.7%, 79.4%, and 84.0%, respectively, while consistently outperforming recent state-of-the-art YOLO-based traffic sign detectors. These findings demonstrate that combining multi-scale receptive fields, channel attention, and enhanced feature fusion enables more accurate and robust traffic sign detection while maintaining the computational efficiency required for real-world deployment.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] A Co-Located MMG-FES Wearable Interface for Action-Updated State-Gated Stimulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Functional electrical stimulation (FES) assists movement, but fixed schedules cannot track how a repeatedly activated muscle changes, and surface electromyography (EMG) near the stimulation electrodes is often obscured by artifacts. Prior work recorded mechanomyography (MMG) passively during closed-loop FES cycling and estimated FES-induced fatigue or predicted fatigue for FES control, without gating stimulation with stimulated-site MMG. In this study, we present VG-FES, a wearable module co-locating microphone-based MMG, programmable charge-balanced biphasic stimulation, and embedded state-gated control at one on-skin thigh site. After each action, we compare rectus femoris (RF) mean power frequency (MPF) with an early-session baseline of the same direction, giving a relative state. A threshold on its window means enables fixed-duration bursts separated by rest periods. During onboard stimulation, MMG remained recordable, whereas near-site EMG was artifact-dominated. Under prolonged external stimulation, cycle-wise MMG tracked an independent local-pressure reference (Spearman rho = 0.968). In leave-one-session-out evaluation on 2284 squat actions (11 sessions, eight participants), MMG-based action segmentation reached an event-detection F1 of 0.923 and direction classification a balanced accuracy of 0.925. Online, over 15.69 min of self-paced squats, one participant received four bursts while MMG acquisition and action monitoring continued. Mechanical feedback from the stimulated site offers wearable FES and assistive robotics a per-action basis for state-gated stimulation.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Diagonal recovery from noisy Fourier--Hermite coefficients: exact orders of the error
item.description: arXiv:2610.15610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the recovery of functions of the weighted Wiener classes $W_s^\mu$ from perturbed Fourier--Hermite coefficients in the metric of $L_\infty(\mathbb R)$. For the summation methods of the class $\mathcal S^\theta$ we find error estimates on $W_s^\mu$. The estimates take into account the behaviour of the Hermite functions both in the oscillatory region and near the turning point: the maxima of functions with different indices are attained at different points, and the supremum of a sum over a block of indices is substantially smaller than the sum of the suprema. Owing to this, in particular, we establish a common lower bound for all finite diagonal methods; for $s\ne4/3$ and $p\ne4/3$ it matches the upper bound and gives the exact order of the error in this class, while at the critical points the gap between the bounds does not exceed $(\log(e/\delta))^{1/4}$ up to a constant. If, in addition, $s>4/3$ or $p<4/3$, then this order is also optimal among all recovery operators that use the whole sequence of data.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Lesion-Aware Attention for Mammography Segmentation with Heterogeneous Supervision
item.description: arXiv:2610.15612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate lesion segmentation in mammography is important for computer-aided breast cancer diagnosis, but dense pixel-level annotations remain costly and limited. Existing public segmentation datasets usually cover only a small set of lesion types with manually delineated masks, whereas larger mammography datasets often provide only image-level diagnostic labels. This annotation mismatch makes it difficult to train segmentation models that can generalize to rare or weakly annotated lesion categories. To address this problem, we study open-vocabulary mammographic lesion segmentation under a mixed-supervision setting, where pixel-level masks are available for base lesion categories and image-level labels are available for a broader set of categories. We propose a two-branch framework that jointly learns from segmentation data and classification data. The segmentation branch learns lesion boundaries from annotated masks, while the classification branch introduces additional image-level semantic supervision. To better transfer image-level supervision to lesion-relevant regions, we further introduce a Lesion-wise Attentive Classifier that maintains category-specific feature prototypes and generates lesion-aware attention maps for foreground feature pooling. This design reduces the influence of background tissue and encourages more compact lesion representations. Experiments on multiple mammography datasets show that the proposed method consistently improves open-vocabulary segmentation baselines on both base and novel lesion categories, while reducing the gap to fully supervised models that require dense target-domain masks. Qualitative results further indicate that our method produces more complete lesion localization for small, low-contrast, and visually subtle mammographic findings.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] ProML: Progressive Multi-label Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.15614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-label learning typically pursues model construction through the joint optimization of label fitting, correlation modeling, and structural regularization. While empirically effective, such a coupled paradigm imposes multiple learning objectives on a single predictive parameter matrix, forcing it to simultaneously fit observed labels and encode structural priors. This coupling may induce ill-conditioned optimization geometry, increase hyper-parameter sensitivity, and complicate capacity control. To address the these issues, this paper proposes a Progressive Multi-Label Learning (ProML) framework, which decouples direct label fitting from predictor learning via the introduction of an auxiliary predictive variable. This auxiliary variable admits a closed-form solution, yielding an equivalent profiled objective in which the supervised fitting term is scaled by a trade-off parameter. This result provides a unified view of ProML and conventional coupled learning, with the latter recovered as a limiting case. We theoretically analyze the optimization geometry of ProML and show that, under quadratic positive semidefinite structural regularization, ProML attenuates the dominant curvature of the fitting term, enlarges the stable learning rate range, and provides a controllable fidelity-regularization trade-off. Further, we instantiate the ProML for multi-label feature selection task by integrating global-local label priors and row-sparse regularization. Extensive experiments and controlled optimization analyses on 12 benchmark datasets empirically corroborate the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the robust and competitive performance of the proposed method.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Generative AI enables human-centered design of sustainable plant-based foods
item.description: arXiv:2610.15616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dietary transitions away from animal-based meat could reduce food-related environmental burdens, but plant-based alternatives must compete on flavor, texture, and overall liking. Here we extend a generative AI framework with 469 plant-based burger recipes and use it to create six formulations across five primary ingredients: bean, chickpea, lentil, mushroom, and oat. An executive chef translates the AI-generated formulations into standardized preparation protocols and refines the ingredient quantities based on culinary expertise. The integration of generative modeling and culinary expertise defines a human-centered generative AI framework for food design. We evaluate the six burgers in a blinded sensory survey with 101 participants in an operating restaurant and quantify their land use, greenhouse gas emissions, eutrophication potential, and scarcity-weighted water use. We use Big Mac scores from a previous survey as an iconic commercial benchmark. The mushroom burger achieves mean flavor, texture, and overall liking scores similar to the Big Mac, with less than one-third of its estimated environmental impact. The other formulations reduce the estimated impact further, in several cases to near one-tenth of the Big Mac value, but receive lower liking scores. Mixed-effects models quantify associations between sensory attributes and human liking and retain predictive accuracy on independent survey data, with mean absolute errors no greater than 0.52 points on a seven-point scale. Together, these results demonstrate how generative design, culinary expertise, human sensory response, and environmental assessment can converge to create sustainable foods that people want to eat.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] From Stages to States: Unified Iterative Reasoning for MLLMs
item.description: arXiv:2610.15620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (MCoT) substantially enhances the complex reasoning capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by explicitly modeling intermediate reasoning processes. However, most learning-based MCoT methods follow a stage-centric paradigm, where different reasoning behaviors are assigned to predefined stages and optimized separately. This results in fragmented reasoning and a training-inference reasoning-state gap. To address these limitations, we propose ReState, a unified iterative reasoning framework that reformulates multimodal reasoning from a stage-driven pipeline into a state-driven dynamic process. It comprises two complementary components: Unified Reasoning State Modeling (URSM) and Closed-Loop Reasoning-State Learning (CRSL). URSM unifies reasoning construction, correct reasoning preservation, and erroneous reasoning correction as reasoning-state transitions within a shared state space, enabling these heterogeneous reasoning behaviors to be learned jointly. CRSL further incorporates self-generated historical reasoning states during training and recursively updates the current state during inference, thereby mitigating the reasoning-state gap and enabling iterative self-refinement without requiring an additional reflection module, critic, or independent correction stage. Furthermore, we construct VersaCoT-10K, a high-quality CoT dataset spanning eight visual reasoning domains, which provides diverse supervision for multi-domain reasoning and reasoning-state refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ReState exhibits strong adaptability across different MLLM backbones and achieves strong performance on multiple public reasoning benchmarks, supporting the shift from stage-centric reasoning toward state-centric reasoning. Our data and code are available at https://github.com/YuChuang1205/ReState
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Adaptive Role Assignment and Controlled Feature Reconstruction for Federated Image Semantic Communication
item.description: arXiv:2610.15623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid federated semantic communication enables user equipment (UEs) to contribute model updates or semantic features under a shared training framework. However, heterogeneous role costs and the interaction between model aggregation and feature reconstruction (FR) remain key challenges in practical radio access network (RAN) deployment. To address these issues, we propose ARC-FedSC, a RAN-aware framework that coordinates UE role assignment and server-side controlled FR under a fixed communication budget. Within ARC-FedSC, RAN Aware Role-Bandit learns the historical contribution of UEs in different roles together with current uplink conditions, while Temporal Consistency Alignment (TCA) regulates FR according to recent model aggregation directions. Experiments on CIFAR-10 with time-varying RAN channels show that ARC-FedSC outperforms baselines across all five tested role configurations in the later training stage, with the best configurations achieving about 24.17 dB average PSNR over the last 20 rounds. Component level results further show that Role-Bandit maintains an average rolling UE coverage of 85.3%, compared with about 65.7% for baseline, while TCA reduces the probability of harmful FR events from 0.245 to 0.093, corresponding to a 62.0% reduction. Ablation and sensitivity studies further support the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed design.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] 1Step-WAM: Your World Action Model but Faster using 1-Step Action Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) unify visual world modeling and action generation, yet their real-world deployment is heavily bottlenecked by iterative action denoising and the sequential execution of visual prefilling and action prediction. We demonstrate that the action-denoising trajectories in WAMs are approximately straight, rendering the first-step velocity a strong estimate of the final action direction. Building on this observation, we introduce 1Step-WAM, a framework that transforms multi-step action denoising into one single forward. Specifically, we employ a lightweight calibrator to directly correct the first step velocity, and use bandwidth-constrained action decoding to further reduce errors in the calibrated one-step actions. Compressing action generation into a single step enables it to execute in parallel with visual prefilling, completely breaking the sequential bottleneck of the traditional imagination-then-action paradigm. Evaluations on RoboTwin and LIBERO show that 1Step-WAM largely preserves multi-step task success with only about 13.4M trainable parameters, while achieving inference speedups of $7.44\times$, $5.98\times$, and $24.84\times$ for FastWAM, ImageWAM and Kairos, respectively. Furthermore, real-world robotic deployments using the FastWAM backbone confirm a consistent 7.44$\times$ speedup while maintaining close success rate to the multi-step baseline. Code is avaliable at https://github.com/changdong1687/1Step-WAM.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Riemannian Suppression of Cross-Session Identity Leakage in Motor-Imagery EEG
item.description: arXiv:2610.15626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) recorded for motor-imagery (MI) brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) carries subject-identifying structure that persists across sessions, allowing separately released sessions from the same person to be linked. Existing EEG identity protections use learned or additive perturbations and operate on representations other than the covariance geometry underlying MI pipelines. We ask whether cross-session identity leakage can be suppressed directly in this covariance representation without learning a privacy model. We introduce a Riemannian transform that equalizes two subject-conditioned geometric statistics: the Riemannian mean covariance and the tangent-space scatter around it, with two optional band-specific refinements. Ablations show that mean alignment and scatter whitening carry nearly all of the suppression, while the optional stages contribute small, dataset-dependent refinements. Across two public datasets and five attackers spanning four covariance-space representations, the worst attacker falls from 90.8% to 15.6% on BCI Competition IV-2a and from 90.8% to 9.9% on OpenBMI, at a cost of 7.0 and 2.1 points of MI decoding accuracy relative to the 8-30 Hz input, and no aggregation rule exceeds chance by more than two points at any batch size. The transform requires no learned privacy model, surrogate network, or gradient-based training, and is fitted on one session and applied unchanged to a held-out later session.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Robust Detection of Directional Adversarial Attacks in Deep Neural Networks for Radiological Imaging
item.description: arXiv:2610.15628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning is now central to radiology, helping detect changes on X-rays, CTs, and MRIs. However, these systems are highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks - small, crafted perturbations that mislead models while appearing unchanged to humans. Such errors risk missed cancers or false positives. Studies show over 90% attack success on medical scans. Almost 30% of US hospitals use AI in imaging in 2023. Thus, an effective method of detecting such attacks and their directionality is crucial to ensure the credibility and reliability of medical systems based on DNNs. We propose a novel detection framework that leverages subsequent attacks using random noise to identify adversarial perturbations. Our approach uses the analysis of variations in the Sigmoid function to distinguish genuine medical images from adversarially manipulated ones. Specifically, we compare prediction differences between clean and attacked images, as well as between different adversarially altered versions, to improve detection accuracy. We evaluated our method on three popular medical datasets including 'Chest X-Ray Images for Classification', 'Retinal Fundus Multi-disease Image Dataset' and 'Brain Tumor Dataset' under various attack scenarios, including random noise. Our framework achieved up to 99.8% ACC in identifying adversarial directional attacks, significantly outperforming existing defense mechanisms. It consistently identified adversarial samples across varying attack strengths while keeping false positives low, showing strong reliability and potential for clinical use. Furthermore, our proposal highlights its potential for real-world deployment.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] The Price of Precision: A Calibrated Cost Model for Mixed-Precision LLM Serving
item.description: arXiv:2610.15629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Choosing a mixed-precision configuration for large language model (LLM) serving trades speed against accuracy. Allocators that use average bit-width or a memory budget as a speed proxy can miss changes in the resource that limits execution. We argue that served speed can be limited by compute, weight loading, or key-value (KV) cache access, depending on the phase, batch size, and context length. A byte-based proxy does not capture all of these costs, so fewer bits do not always mean faster serving. To address this gap, we build a cost model that accounts for the binding resource and use it in two ways. First, as a predictor: given a configuration and operating point, it estimates serving latency using constants calibrated for the model, GPU, and serving stack. We evaluate its accuracy across three hardware classes. Second, as an allocator: we combine modeled time costs with measured per-tensor accuracy costs and use a dynamic program to select a configuration under a latency or accuracy budget. We compare its configurations against byte-aware and sensitivity-only allocation.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Binary Codes Correcting Multiple Edits via Polynomial Hashing and Entropy Recycling
item.description: arXiv:2610.15631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Codes in the Levenshtein metric that can correct multiple edits (including deletions, insertions, and substitutions) have attracted a lot of attention recently owing to their application in DNA-based storage and racetrack memories. In this work, we present new techniques for designing explicit binary codes of length $n$ that correct $t$ edits with at most $(2t+1)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. We first propose to use a polynomial hash to construct a systematic code that corrects $t$ edits with $(4t+2)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. Then we observe that there are many polynomial hashes like this, some are good, some are bad. So, we propose the second technique, called entropy recycling, to use the indices of good hashes to carry information. As a consequence, we obtain a partial-systematic code of length $n$ that corrects $t$ edits with at most $(2t+1)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. Finally, we provide deterministic polynomial-time encoding and decoding algorithms for our code.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Towards Finite Satisfiability of PDL with Loops
item.description: arXiv:2610.15632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) is a well-established modal logic of programs. Among its many extensions, the loop operator stands out for capturing the cyclic behaviour of programs: a world satisfies loop(pi) precisely when it can return to itself along a path matching the regular expression pi. While the satisfiability problem for the resulting logic LPDL was settled already in the 1980s, the decidability of its finite satisfiability problem has remained open ever since. The core difficulty is inherent to the finite setting: requiring and forbidding cycles at once is easily reconciled over arbitrary models, but over finite ones it defeats the existing finite-model-theoretic techniques. We make the first substantial progress towards closing this gap. We prove that finite satisfiability is ExpTime-complete for LPDL formulae (also in the presence of the converse operator) in negation normal form, under the restriction that every negated non-atomic loop has the form loop(pi^+) for some arbitrarily complex program pi -- a generalised form of self-reachability; positive occurrences of loops remain unrestricted. At the heart of our approach lies a novel way of representing intended finite models as their infinite, cactus-like unravellings: these are recognisable by two-way tree automata and satisfy a tailored omega-regular foldability condition that lets us finitise the accepted structures.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Big-Big-SycoBench: A Benchmark to Detect Sycophancy Through Model Responses to Valid vs. Invalid Arguments
item.description: arXiv:2610.15634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sycophancy in large language models risks amplifying unsupported claims or beliefs across the knowledge ecosystem as these systems increasingly contribute to research synthesis, evaluation, and decision-making. A reliable model should revise its judgement when a user identifies a genuine flaw, but should resist pushback based on fallacies, emotion, or irrelevant appeals to authority. While sycophancy is usually measured on questions with a verifiable answer, the evaluative tasks in which it is most difficult to detect have no such ground truth. We introduce Big-Big-SycoBench, which measures sycophancy through argument discernment: the ability to revise an evaluation after valid criticism while resisting invalid pressure. The benchmark consists of 450 text artefacts with 5,400 arguments for raising or lowering their quality scores, each reviewed by one or more of twelve human annotators. An LLM scores each artefact twenty times to establish its baseline score and uncertainty. The model is then given a valid or invalid argument and asked to update its score. We only count a revision if it exceeds the model's own baseline variability. We use the resulting score delta to distinguish responsiveness to valid arguments from compliance with invalid ones. Across ten models, responsiveness is 88-95\% for seven, 76-77\% for Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, and 32\% for Opus 5.5. Compliance ranges from 0.2\% for GPT-6 Astra to 95\% for GPT-4o. Big-Big-SycoBench is intended to guide the development of models whose judgements can be corrected by sound arguments, but not displaced by unsupported pressure.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] MERIT: Scaling KG Foundation Models with Relation Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2610.15638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge graph (KG) foundation models (KGFMs) predict links on unseen graphs zero-shot. KGFMs have been pioneered by ULTRA which builds a relation graph from co-occurrences that match motif templates, and passes messages over it to obtain relation representations. More recent KGFMs such as MOTIF and TRIX increase the size of this relation graph, and FLOCK replaces message-passing with probabilistic random-walk ensembles. However, larger relation graphs mean more messages, and more walks mean more sequences to encode, so they improve performance at higher training and inference cost. This cost hinders their use in more complex reasoning tasks, such as complex query answering. To reverse this trend, we design MERIT, the first KGFM with a transformer relation encoder: every relation name attends to every other, and the motifs enter as a soft prior rather than as edges. Over 56 benchmarks, MERIT matches the zero-shot MRR of SoTA KGFMs while being 6x faster than TRIX and over 100x faster than FLOCK at inference. Fine-tuned for complex query answering like UltraQuery, MERITQuery improves over it at matched cost.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Imitation Learning via Discrete and Rhythmic Primitive Composition
item.description: arXiv:2610.15639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation is inherently composed of semantically meaningful sub-tasks. While Movement Primitives (MPs) can model these components, their composition typically relies on manual engineering or sample-inefficient reinforcement learning. Existing supervised methods are limited by the lack of MP labels in standard datasets and often fail to generalize across discrete and rhythmic movements. We propose Neural Dynamic Composition (NDC), a supervised framework to compose Dynamic Movement Primitives (DMPs) using only raw trajectories for supervision, given a single example of each primitive. Our approach exploits parallel combinations of DMPs as a differentiable relaxation of categorical primitive selection, and utilizes a warp-invariant loss formulation to identify primitives despite spatial or temporal variations. A staged training curriculum is employed to learn the selection policy and DMP parameters, unifying discrete and rhythmic movements in one framework. Evaluated on 2D handwriting and 3D robotic tasks, our method outperforms baselines on most tasks and metrics. An ablation study demonstrates how each design choice contributes to the system's performance.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Context-Aware Precision Scheduling for Small Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.15640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small language models (SLMs) used as on-device agents must balance accuracy and latency as their context grows. Mixed precision helps manage this tradeoff by assigning different precisions to weight tensors according to their size and sensitivity. However, these choices depend on the operating conditions, so a configuration selected for a short context may no longer provide the best tradeoff at a longer one. We calibrate a timing model from measurements at different precisions and context lengths, and combine it with tensor sensitivities to choose configurations under a latency or accuracy budget. We argue that fewer bits do not always mean faster execution, so our predictor estimates latency from calibrated execution costs rather than weight bytes alone. Under a latency budget, reading the larger key-value (KV) cache leaves less time for weight operations, leading the allocator to select lower precisions. This gives a schedule of tensor changes that can be prepared before execution. Our runtime follows the schedule while retaining the session's KV cache. We evaluate executed schedules on a laptop GPU, including a longer-context schedule with three weight formats and a tool-use benchmark measuring full response time and correctness. Under an accuracy budget, measured error from a quantized KV cache determines the budget left for weights. The allocator can raise or lower weight precision as this estimate changes. These experiments show where context-aware precision helps and where accuracy recovery remains limited.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Recall What Is Missing: Composing Evidence from Long-Term Agent Memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.15642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under a limited context budget, a long-term agent must recall not merely memories that are individually relevant, but evidence that is collectively sufficient for the current query. Conventional memory access retrieves, scores, and truncates memories, often spending multiple context slots on redundant facts while leaving complementary evidence behind. We cast the read phase of long-term memory as query-conditioned evidence composition: each memory is valued by what it adds beyond the evidence already selected. We instantiate this operation with MemPursuit, a training-free mechanism that uses the residual of a sparse convex query reconstruction as a representation-space proxy for what the current memory set is missing. By reusing the query and candidate embeddings already available from retrieval, MemPursuit progressively composes nested evidence contexts without invoking a language model or cross-encoder to score each query--memory pair. The effectiveness of our method is verified on 3 popular benchmarks in comparison to strong baselines. In fixed-budget LoCoMo experiments, MemPursuit improves end-to-end accuracy by 7.2 percentage points at Top-10 and 5.5 percentage points at Top-20, with consistent gains across multiple memory frameworks, while achieving a 32.9$\times$ speedup in median reranking latency over fully batched BGE-v2-m3. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/FengQi-HITSZ/MemPursuit.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] SurgCast: Action-Conditioned Future Skeletons for Controllable Surgical World Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.15645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surgical world models must turn prospective robot actions into visually faithful, structurally consistent instrument motion. We introduce SurgCast, which predicts future instrument skeletons from current structure, robot state, and future actions, then uses the forecast to control video generation. Dual-path injection combines skeleton geometry with derived, instrument-specific motion descriptors through geometric residuals and conditioning modulation. Both paths complement native action conditioning and are retained in a four-step causal student. On SutureBot and SRTH-Porcine-Cholei, the teacher and student improve all seven reported quality and instrument-consistency metrics over their respective direct-action baselines; teacher FVD decreases by 37.6% and 67.3%. Ablations show that future actions improve skeleton prediction and that combining both injection paths performs best across all six metrics under predicted skeletons. These results support using predicted articulated structure and its motion semantics as a control interface for surgical video prediction. Project videos and examples are available at https://surgcast.netlify.app/.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Distributed Economic Dispatch Scheme of A BESS Network with A Switching Utility Grid in Energy Internet Paradigm via Reset Consensus Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.15647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article aims to design a distributed economic dispatch (ED) scheme based on marginal cost (MC) consensus for a battery energy storage system (BESS) network considering the utility grid switching. Due to the low control accuracy and slow convergence speed of previous schemes, some important changes have been made in this article. Firstly, the feedback coupling term is introduced into the closed-loop error to further improve the stability and convergence rate of the controller. Then, a proportional integral (PI) controller with a reset mechanism is implemented in the designed scheme, which improves the speed and control accuracy of MC consensus. The performance of a control system with a reset mechanism is well guaranteed by analyzing the eigenvalues of the corresponding matrix. Finally, some tests focus on UG switching, time phased pricing, load switching, a BESS/agent plug and play, and large-scale system applications to illustrate the effectiveness and progressiveness of the design scheme.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Transport Polynomial Exactness for Direct ALE-DG Methods with Nonsmooth mesh motion: A Conservative Coefficient-Evolution Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.15650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-order direct arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian discontinuous Galerkin (ALE-DG) methods can suffer severe order reduction under nonsmooth mesh motion despite satisfying the geometric conservation law (GCL). To address this limitation, we propose a new ALE-DG framework applicable to moving triangular and quadrilateral meshes. This framework successfully overcomes the uniform Lipschitz constraint inherent in existing direct ALE-DG methods, retaining high-order accuracy even when the mesh-velocity gradients are unbounded. This capability is driven by transport polynomial exactness (TPE($k$)), which is a structural property stronger than the GCL. TPE($k$) ensures the exact transport of polynomials of degree at most $k$ under arbitrary mesh motion. To incorporate TPE($k$) into a direct ALE-DG method, we introduce a coefficient-evolution (CE) formulation. Reconciling strict local conservation, an indispensable requirement for accurate shock capturing, with the preservation of the TPE(\(k\)) property constitutes the principal technical challenge. We resolve this by evolving the coefficients using the third-order strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta method, paired with a conservative correction executed via Simpson's rule integration. Crucially, this correction strictly vanishes for exactly transported quadratic polynomials, thereby ensuring that our third-order scheme rigorously satisfies the TPE($2$) property. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed scheme retains third-order accuracy when the discrete mesh-velocity Lipschitz estimate grows as $\mathcal O(h^{-1})$, whereas a representative existing direct ALE-DG scheme exhibits order reduction under the same mesh motion. Tests with discontinuous solutions further demonstrate robust and high-resolution performance under random and Lagrangian mesh motions.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Learned Graph Bases for Neural Operators on Power-System Transients
item.description: arXiv:2610.15651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fourier neural operators predict power-system transient trajectories with high accuracy. We extend this line of work by examining the choice of spatial spectral basis, studying both the graph Fourier transform derived from the grid's own coupling network and learnable bases trained from that starting point and from a Fourier control. Evaluated in one controlled pipeline across three protocols spanning unseen fault locations and shifted operating regimes, the learnable bases improve on a parameter- and budget-matched DFT variant by 7-14% in distribution, with per-case significance on both in-distribution protocols and no loss on the third; the gain comes from adaptation rather than from the coordinates alone. We further characterize the regime dependence of this gain, identifying its cause, locus, and continuity, and show that a resolution requires no new model: averaging the learned and frozen variants gives the best shift-robust predictor, while their disagreement provides a label-free alarm that flags every shifted case with no false alarms.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Saving the Queen is hard: Hive is EXPTIME-complete
item.description: arXiv:2610.15654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hive is a boardless two-player strategy game in which the pieces form the playing surface. We prove that deciding whether White can force a win in single-Queen $n$-Hive, the generalization with exactly one Queen Bee per player, is EXPTIME-complete, even when all pieces are already placed. Our hardness proof reduces from unbounded two-player Constraint Logic: Grasshoppers encode edge orientations, while the One Hive rule enforces the vertex constraints. We obtain the EXPTIME upper bound by considering positions up to translation. The result answers the single-Queen question raised by Andel and Rin. Keeping the same inventory and movement rules, it also gives EXPTIME-completeness for multi-Queen variants. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first use of unbounded two-player Constraint Logic to prove EXPTIME-completeness for a natural problem.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Exact Sampling Under Campbell Cost via R\'enyi Channel Simulation Divergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.15656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the communication cost of exact sampling under Campbell's exponential coding criterion. Given a target distribution $P$ and a proposal distribution $Q$, the sender and receiver share i.i.d. $Q$-distributed samples, and the sender communicates an index so that the selected sample has distribution exactly $P$. We introduce a new information measure R\'enyi channel simulation divergence $R_\alpha(P\Vert Q)$, a R\'enyi generalization of the channel simulation divergence. We then show that it lower bounds the Campbell cost of every exact sampler and is achievable, via a new layered sampling scheme, within an additive constant depending only on the Campbell parameter. This yields a tighter one-shot characterization than previous bounds based on R\'enyi divergences of different orders. For i.i.d. product distributions, under suitable non-degeneracy and moment conditions, we further show that the gap beyond the leading R\'enyi-divergence term is $\frac{1}{2}\log n+O(1)$.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Dynamic Conflict Clustering with Lightweight Learning and Strategic Repair for Distributed Constraint Satisfaction
item.description: arXiv:2610.15658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed Constraint Satisfaction Problems (DCSPs) model distributed decision-making in multi-agent systems, where agents assign values to local variables while satisfying shared constraints. However, many DCSP solvers still rely on broad, repeated peer-to-peer communication and are largely reactive, with limited support for strategic coordination or learning. This increases communication overhead, can lead to stagnation, and reduces the success of hard instances. Hence, we propose Dynamic Conflict Clustering-Incomplete (DCC-Incomplete), a repair-based solver that combines conflict-centred decomposition, structured coordination, strategic repair, and lightweight learning for stagnation recovery. DCC-Incomplete groups the unsolved part of the problem into conflict clusters and restricts communication via a coordination layer to agents within the same conflict region. It also introduces memory-guided restart, enabling agents and clusters to pause, revise, and adapt repairs based on neighbouring conflict states. A thorough evaluation of DCC-Incomplete on distributed graph-colouring benchmarks with planted satisfying assignments shows that its memory-guided restart improves the success rate from 37.50% to 61.11%, reduces median runtime from 0.565s to 0.367s, and cuts median communication from 12.493 to 6.503 messages per constraint. These results suggest that dynamic conflict clustering, combined with lightweight strategic and learning-guided repair, improves both communication efficiency and robustness in incomplete DCSP solving.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Testing Central Structure for Complex Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.15659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Centrality measures rank nodes even when the observed differences can be explained by ordinary structural variation. We therefore study a preceding question: whether a network contains a statistically identifiable central structure at all. We formulate this question as a network-level hypothesis testing issue using the adjacency spectral radius as the test statistic and estimate an empirical p-value from randomized networks generated under a specified null model. The framework is evaluated using G(N,M), Chung-Lu, and two implementations of the configuration model on simulated benchmarks and 55 real networks. Controlled experiments further vary the number and connection weights of designated central nodes while holding network size and density fixed. The results show a clear negative association between central-structure strength and the empirical p-value. They also demonstrate that rejection decisions depend substantially on the structural properties preserved by the null model: the detected network sets are not simply nested across models.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Sparse All-Layer Connector for Domain Generalised Semantic Segmentation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Domain generalised semantic segmentation (DGSS) has recently benefited from combining multiple foundation models, such as vision-language and vision foundation models, to leverage their diverse representations for generalisation. Existing multi-model approaches share a common design choice: cross-model fusion is restricted to depth-aligned layers, implicitly assuming that mutually beneficial information resides at the same depth across models. However, foundation models pretrained under different objectives may develop distinct representation hierarchies, making the optimality of depth-aligned fusion questionable. Moreover, we observe that the foundation models exhibit different depth-wise domain sensitivity. Motivated by these observations, we propose a Sparse All-Layer Connector (SALC) that enables each layer to access information from preceding layers of another model. As the number of accessible layers grows with depth, dense aggregation may hurt generalisation. SALC therefore learns to adaptively select a sparse subset of informative layers. We further introduce a candidate dropout regularisation that strengthens sparsity and encourages SALC to explore diverse layers, leading to more robust selection. Across four foundation model combinations and three DGSS evaluation settings, the proposed design demonstrates stronger generalisation than conventional depth-aligned fusion. The code is available at https://github.com/RuoyuGuo/SALC.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Feedback as an Interface: Controlling Form and Detail in LLM Translation Refinement
item.description: arXiv:2610.15661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feedback presentation shapes how LLMs use evaluator judgments during translation refinement. We introduce a machine translation protocol that keeps the evaluator score, main issue, and recommendation fixed while varying feedback form and supporting detail. Across seven models and six translation directions, low-load feedback outperforms high-load feedback in all 42 translator-direction settings under xCOMET. On the 29,400-record rewriting subset, mean xCOMET scores multiplied by 100 are 83.30 for low-load feedback and 80.67 for high-load feedback; the full-matrix original-translation reference mean is 83.46. MetricX-24 supports the low-load advantage on a stratified subset. A no-feedback second pass yields a small improvement over the original translations, and direct evaluator prompting reproduces the low-load advantage without a separate rewriting stage. These results show that compact feedback limits the quality loss from evaluator-guided refinement in the evaluated high-resource MT settings.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] Drift, Then Spread: Learning One-Step Generative Policies for Online Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.15662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative policies offer expressive action distributions for online reinforcement learning (RL), but many diffusion- and flow-based policies require costly iterative sampling. We propose DriftSpread, a one-step generative policy based on Drifting for online maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) RL. To incorporate entropy without a tractable policy density, we build on an energy-based view of Drifting and derive critic-guided Drift and entropy-induced Spread from the negative MaxEnt objective. Our method learns these updates sequentially in the same actor, using action regression for value improvement and distribution matching to capture the effect of entropy. The actor updates require neither direct samples from the critic-defined Boltzmann target nor policy-density or score estimation. Under exact fitting with a fixed critic, we prove convergence to the Boltzmann target in the small-step limit followed by the long-time limit. On MuJoCo, DriftSpread achieves the highest aggregate normalized return among all evaluated methods, while outperforming the diffusion- and flow-based baselines in both training and inference efficiency.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] A simplified proof of polynomial improvements for 3SUM and APSP
item.description: arXiv:2610.15663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a simplified proof of the polynomial improvements for integer 3SUM and all-pairs shortest paths (APSP) established by Alman and Vassilevska Williams, with weaker exponents. The central ingredient is selected-entry matrix multiplication: computing a prescribed set of entries of a product of dense rectangular matrices. Starting from Sch\"onhage's inner/outer-product identity, we construct a multiplication rule that shares intermediate products among many outputs. We apply this rule recursively and bound the work by counting the requested entries at each level. Applied to incidence matrices, the algorithm solves Offline Set Disjointness over a small universe. Known deterministic reductions then yield truly subquadratic integer 3SUM and truly subcubic APSP for polynomially bounded integer inputs.
item.author: cs updates on arXiv.org

item.title: [cs updates on arXiv.org] AnyEdit: A Unified Framework for Speech and Singing Voice Editing with Real-World Environmental Consistency
item.description: arXiv:2610.15665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present AnyEdit, a unified, separation-free framework for speech and singing voice editing that preserves real-world acoustic environments, including noise, reverberation, and background music. Recent unified generative models already achieve strong speech and singing generation in clean conditions, but real-world vocal editing remains challenging because the model must revise content while simultaneously preserving speaker identity, prosody, and the surrounding acoustic scene. Directly modeling noisy audio end-to-end entangles semantic editing with environmental acoustics, weakening the core vocal generation capability. We therefore adopt a two-stage design that preserves clean-domain editing ability while deferring acoustic rendering to a separate stage: an instruction-guided autoregressive editor first predicts clean prosody and content-style tokens, supported by a teacher-student noise-robust prosody tokenizer that distills clean prosodic tokens from degraded recordings; a flow-matching acoustic model then performs in-context rendering conditioned on the source acoustic context, so the edited segment inherits surrounding noise, reverberation, and background sound while maintaining consistent speaker timbre. To stabilize unedited regions, we introduce unmodified-area-aware supervision; after pre-training, we further apply direct preference optimization on mined real-to-real singing pairs. We also release AnyEditBench, a benchmark covering both speech and singing voice editing under clean, simulated, and in-the-wild acoustic conditions. Experiments on Chinese and English speech and singing datasets showed that AnyEdit consistently outperforms strong baselines in content accuracy, subjective quality, and background consistency under noisy and reverberant conditions. Demo: https://any-edit.github.io/. AnyEditBench: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Ririiiii/anyeditbench.
